# Musical Theatre Source Census Repair

The repaired source register below replaces fragile citation-marker references with stable plain-text Source IDs and raw URLs. It also repairs the earlier batch problem by giving MT-B2 a formal source set made up of verified exam-board, syllabus, adjudication, and common-standard comparator sources, while keeping degree-level admissions material in MT-B1 and practitioner/casting guidance in MT-B3. Official short-course and pedagogy material from RADA and Guildhall remain in MT-B4, not MT-B1. citeturn23search0turn22search0turn24search4turn24search6turn23search3turn25search0turn26search1turn26search2turn27search2turn28search2turn13search0turn13search2

## Executive summary

This discovery pass establishes a discovery-level source universe for Musical Theatre audition assessment and organises it into four research batches. Across the public web, I located official or high-authority sources spanning UK conservatoires, US Musical Theatre programmes, exam boards, the sector-wide Musical Theatre Common Prescreen material, and casting/practitioner guidance. The strongest discovery cluster is **official admissions/audition guidance**; the strongest explicit-assessment cluster is **exam-board syllabi**. Casting-body material is thinner and more general, with the clearest official UK body source being the **Casting Directors’ Guild** on self-tapes rather than a Musical Theatre-specific rubric. citeturn32search1turn28search5turn29search2

At discovery level, every **mandatory named source** has now been assigned a status: **LAMDA, Trinity College London, Mountview, Bird College, AMDA, Boston Conservatory/BoCo, and the CDG/comparable casting guidance were located**; **RADA was located but appears more relevant here through short-course/audition-training or adjacent material than through a degree-level MT admissions rubric**; **Guildhall remains unresolved for MT-specific public audition criteria in this pass**. That means the mandatory source universe is covered for census purposes even where some items still need full extraction in later batches. citeturn6search3turn28search5turn32search1

The pages already reviewed show that the later analysis stages should expect to capture at least these recurring evidence areas: repertoire era/style splits (for example legit/pre-1965 versus contemporary/post-1965), acting–voice–dance integration, self-tape setup expectations, quick redirection/adaptability, individuality/authenticity, and signs of professional readiness or training potential. Explicit subtype labelling for **Golden Age, contemporary MT, pop/rock, dance-led, actor-musician, and style/genre contrasts** appears in several institutional sources, but **jukebox** and **through-composed** are not commonly surfaced as stand-alone assessment categories on public admissions pages discovered so far. citeturn14search0turn7search2turn21search0turn18search2turn17search2

## Proposed batch plan

### MT-B1

**Official institutions and admissions.**  
This batch should extract explicit audition requirements, repertoire rules, dance-call expectations, self-tape instructions, interview/recall structure, and any published “what we are looking for” language from the main conservatoire and programme pages. Priority targets: LAMDA, Mountview, Bird, ArtsEd, RWCMD, RCS, GSA, Leeds, Urdang, AMDA, BoCo, University of Michigan, CCM, Carnegie Mellon, Penn State, Shenandoah, Pace, NYU Tisch, and Associated Studios. citeturn6search3turn7search2turn8search0turn14search0turn23search0turn24search0

### MT-B2

**Exam boards, syllabi and adjudication.**  
This batch should review LAMDA Exams, Trinity College London, RSL Awards, and the MT Common Prescreen for explicit assessment criteria, mark bands, learning outcomes, and the way acting/singing/movement integration is described. citeturn28search1turn28search5turn29search2turn25search2

### MT-B3

**Casting, practitioner and industry guidance.**  
This batch should review CDG material, Spotlight practitioner guidance, and selected Playbill casting-director interviews for signals about individuality, preparedness, authenticity, collaboration, repertoire choice, first impressions, and professional conduct in auditions/self-tapes. citeturn32search1turn31search5turn30search0turn30search2

### MT-B4

**Subtype and gap-fill sources.**  
This batch should mine curriculum and guidance pages for clues about style or subtype differences: legit versus contemporary, Golden Age versus post-1970, pop/rock emphasis, actor-musicianship, multiple dance forms, acting-through-song, and training-potential versus ready-made castability. Priority pages include LAMDA MA, Leeds top tips, University of Michigan guidelines, Shenandoah’s programme page, BWMT curriculum, Urdang’s degree framing, and RADA’s MT-adjacent page. citeturn6search3turn12search0turn18search2turn21search4turn27search1turn15search1

## Handoff for MT-B1

MT-B1 should be treated as the **core admissions-and-auditions evidence batch**. The job is not yet to recommend rubric changes, but to extract what institutions explicitly ask for, what they explicitly value, and where they imply criteria through structure. Priority institutions are: **LAMDA, Mountview, Bird, ArtsEd, RWCMD, RCS, GSA, Leeds, Urdang, AMDA, BoCo, University of Michigan, CCM, Carnegie Mellon, Penn State, Shenandoah, Pace, NYU Tisch**, with Associated Studios as a useful vocational comparator. citeturn6search3turn7search2turn8search0turn14search0turn23search0turn24search0

For each source, extract in separate fields:

- **Explicit assessment criteria**: any direct statements such as “we value…”, “we are looking for…”, “evaluation includes…”, or identified audition dimensions.  
- **Implied criteria from requirements**: song era/style splits, monologue rules, dance format, self-tape framing/audio requirements, redirection, recall tasks, interview tasks, devised work, wildcard/personal statement requests.  
- **Training potential vs finished product**: any language about raw talent, potential, willingness to take direction, risk-taking, collaboration, or who the programme is for.  
- **Integration markers**: places where acting, singing and movement are explicitly integrated rather than treated as separate silos.  
- **Subtype/style markers**: legit/pre-1965, contemporary/post-1965, pop/rock, actor-musician, dance-led, or any other style distinctions.  
- **Professional-readiness markers**: audition technique, repertoire development, showcase/career prep, industry alignment, or collaboration norms.

Tag every finding as one of: **explicit criterion**, **implied criterion**, **pedagogic framing**, or **process requirement**. Preserve exact wording where concise, but avoid premature synthesis. If a page is mainly marketing copy, mark it as such rather than over-inferring. If a school’s public page does not state what it values, record that absence clearly.# MT-B1 Remaining Official Institution Rows Completion

## Revised Reusable Handoff Pack for MT-B2

### MT-B1 completion summary

MT-B1 is now complete. The prior gap concerned four queued rows: Italia Conti CertHE Musical Theatre, Italia Conti FdA Musical Theatre, Royal Academy of Music Musical Theatre Audition Requirements, and the Royal Academy of Music Musical Theatre department page. All four have now been re-found, verified, and extracted.

The most important change is that **Italia Conti is no longer under-extracted**. Its current public CertHE and FdA pages now give explicit first-round and recall structures: contemporary British speech, song showing vocal and performance ability, set technical dance plus preferred-style solo, on-site recall, Golden Age versus post-1965 song contrast, recall dance classes, and interview. They also publish unusually useful signals around **acting while singing**, **voice/casting-type suitability**, **response to direction**, **dance assessability**, **reasonable adjustments**, and **audition-based level fit / non-standard entry**.

**Royal Academy of Music is also now complete and confirmed as genuine in MT-B1**, not a mistaken substitute for RADA. The audition-requirements page is valuable because it publishes a distinctive postgraduate video portfolio structure: three songs showing different voice qualities, vocal-range capture, a contemporary naturalistic monologue, a spontaneous motivation video, an unscripted personal-response clip, slate, and embedded self-tape advice. The department page remains a **context source**, not a public scoring rubric, but it is relevant for individuality, diversity, current-practitioner training, and industry-facing readiness.

The main MT-B1 evidence base is therefore broader and cleaner than before. The strongest official-institution sources remain Mountview’s digital handbook, Bird’s applications page, ArtsEd auditions, RWCMD guidance, RCS, Boston Conservatory, CCM best practices, NYU Tisch, Penn State, and now the completed Italia Conti and RAM rows. MT-B2 should not repeat this institutional work. It should now target the remaining public gap: **formal descriptor language, mark bands, adjudication vocabulary, and exam-board grading logic** for acting-through-song, vocal communication versus technique, movement assessment, and interpretation.

  Superseded by current public GSA pages at:  
  https://gsauk.org/auditions-interviews  
  https://gsauk.org/courses/ba-hons-musical-theatre

**No remaining MT-B1 rows are inaccessible, not found, provenance unclear, or still queued.**

### Strongest official-institution findings to carry forward

- **Mountview** — explicit acting-through-song, legit versus contemporary contrast, full-body dance assessability, and recall expansion.
- **Bird** — unusually clear “current and potential skills” plus interview qualities: motivation, communication, flexibility.
- **ArtsEd** — one of the clearest public dance-room criteria sources: how you learn, listen, respond to instruction, and act through dance.
- **RWCMD** — strongest public values language around inhabiting character, risk, generosity, and fair technical consideration.
- **Italia Conti** — now a strong official source for Golden Age versus post-1965 contrast, acting-as-singing, direction-response, dance visibility, interview, and audition-based level fit.
- **Royal Academy of Music** — useful PG comparator for voice-quality contrast, vocal-range capture, naturalistic monologue, motivation/personhood-to-camera, and self-tape standards.
- **CCM** — clearest public vocabulary for vocal ability, physical awareness, communication skills, personality, and development of style.
- **NYU Tisch** — strongest integrated acting / singing / dance / conversation model.
- **Penn State** — explicit distinction between “professional potential” and “perfect casting decision”.

### MT-B2 gaps to resolve through exam boards / syllabi / adjudication

MT-B2 should now target the areas that institutional admissions pages still leave thin:

- formal **mark bands / descriptor language**
- explicit adjudication wording for **acting-through-song**
- clearer separation of **technical vocal execution** from **communication / storytelling**
- more formal grading language for **dance / movement assessment**
- exam-board handling of **individuality / interpretation / professionalism**
- any public descriptor language that can anchor later score calibration without inventing new rubric fields# Musical Theatre MT-B2 Source ID Repair and Completion

## Reusable handoff pack for MT-B3

### MT-B2 completion summary

MT-B2 is complete. All 11 repaired MT-B2 rows now have final statuses. The strongest descriptor-rich exam-board sources were [MT-S004] Trinity College London, [MT-S006] LCME Musical Theatre for Actors, [MT-S007] LCME Musical Theatre for Singers, and [MT-S009] the current RSL/STAGESCHOOL Musical Theatre syllabus. Together, these sources provide the clearest public language for acting-through-song, vocal technique versus communication, movement/storytelling integration, contextual understanding, and how formal assessment frameworks separate performance, technique and reflection. citeturn38view0turn38view6turn28view2turn28view4turn41view2turn41view4

LAMDA remains important and is now fully extracted for criteria, but the most usable surfaced evidence in this run was richer on learning outcomes and assessment criteria than on directly exposed numeric thresholds. [MT-S001] and [MT-S002] are still valuable because they formalise solo/duo interpretation, vocal response, physical response, context/technique knowledge, and group interaction/timing as assessable MT dimensions. citeturn40view0turn40view4turn39view1turn40view5

LCME adds a particularly important distinction: the exam board explicitly separates actor-led and singer-led MT routes. That makes [MT-S005]–[MT-S008] especially useful for later work about route-sensitive wording without assuming a single MT mode. RSL adds current clear attainment bands and section weighting, while Acceptd’s [MT-S011] is now cleanly classified as a **common-standard comparator only**. It standardises submission and comparability, but it is not an awarding-body specification and must not be treated as a scoring rubric. citeturn31view0turn26view4turn41view0turn35view0

The main gap left after MT-B2 is not formal grading language but practitioner and industry judgement: authenticity, first impressions, self-tape fairness, commercial/professional expectations, responsiveness to direction, and how casting-facing feedback differs from educational assessment. MT-B3 should now address that gap using the repaired practitioner/industry pack only. citeturn35view0turn41view4

### LCME completion summary

LCME is now complete across route logic, actors, singers and diplomas. The major takeaway is that LCME explicitly distinguishes actor-led and singer-led MT rather than forcing one framework to cover both. Actor route evidence is strongest for lyric/storytelling and spoken-sung performance; singer route evidence is strongest for domain separation and within-component weighting; diploma evidence is strongest for advanced performance, musicality and contextual presentation.

### Acceptd / MTCP classification summary

[MT-S011] is complete and classified only as **common prescreen standard / submission-standard comparator**. It standardises component menus, timing, framing and submission conventions, but it is not an exam-board specification, awarding-body syllabus or scoring rubric. citeturn35view0

### Gaps for MT-B3

MT-B3 should now target what exam boards do not answer well:
- casting/practitioner views on authenticity and individuality
- self-tape fairness, access and turnaround expectations
- first-impression and professional-behaviour expectations
- responsiveness to direction and risk in audition rooms
- how practitioner judgement differs from educational grading

## Batch scope

The MT-B2 handoff in this conversation explicitly pointed to LAMDA, Trinity, and “additional official MT exam-board documents” plus “common prescreen standards”. Using only the source universe visible in the handoff and the official sources re-found on the public web, this run treats the following eight sources as the MT-B2 batch: LAMDA Solo/Duo, LAMDA Group, Trinity College London, LCME Musical Theatre for Singers, LCME Musical Theatre for Actors, LCME Musical Theatre Diplomas, RSL/PAA Musical Theatre, and Acceptd’s Musical Theater Common Prescreen. ## Batch-Level Findings

Recurring exam-board themes are now much clearer than in MT-B1. Across LAMDA, Trinity, LCME and RSL, the repeated assessment pattern is: technical control, interpretative decision-making, contextual knowledge, and communication/audience engagement. Trinity names those areas through technical skills, engagement with material, and audience awareness; LCME uses technical accomplishment, interpretation, knowledge/understanding and communication; RSL splits acting/singing/dancing criteria but still grades performance, technique, and understanding/reflection. citeturn27view8turn12view3turn14view0turn18view1turn28view4turn25view4

The difference from admissions frameworks is substantial. These exam-board sources publish formal learning outcomes, task structures, explicit attainment bands, and component/domain weightings; admissions pages usually publish tasks and institutional values but much less public scoring logic. Trinity, LCME and RSL all state mark bands or percentage bands openly, and several also explain how reflection/discussion contributes to the result. citeturn31view0turn27view9turn27view15turn14view0turn18view1turn25view3

Integration across acting, voice and movement is central, but the sources do not all organise it the same way. LAMDA Solo/Duo and Group are strongly “acting-through-song” frameworks; Trinity is fully integrated and extends into solo, pair, group, and production modes; LCME deliberately separates singer-led and actor-led routes at grade level, then reunifies them in the 2025 diploma; RSL is group-led overall but adds an individual technical specialism at higher grades; Acceptd separates songs, monologues, dance, ballet and wild card into discrete prescreen assets. citeturn26search0turn26search1turn31view0turn15search2turn15search3turn15search0turn25view1turn29view0turn29view1turn29view2

The strongest descriptor language in this batch comes from Trinity, LCME Actors, LCME Diplomas, and RSL. Those sources most clearly describe what Distinction/Merit/Pass look like in terms of audibility, projection, characterisation, contextual knowledge, engagement, movement use, interpretative truth, and reflection quality. citeturn27view10turn27view17turn27view18turn27view19turn28view2turn28view4

## Evidence Gaps Discovered

The batch still leaves some gaps, but they are now narrower and better defined.

First, subtype calibration remains uneven. Acceptd explicitly references pre/post-1970 contrast and examples such as belt versus head/falsetto mix, and LCME Diplomas lists genres such as Golden Age, jukebox and sung-through, but the exam-board sources do not consistently publish fine-grained public descriptors for, for example, legit versus belt, Golden Age acting conventions versus contemporary speech-song, or dance-style-specific thresholds at the level many admissions panels use informally. citeturn29view0turn16view0

Second, professional-readiness and casting-suitability language is much thinner than assessment language. The exam boards measure performance quality, interpretation, contextual understanding, communication, and reflection; they rarely publish anything like “castability”, role fit, or industry readiness as a formal criterion. That contrasts with parts of MT-B1. citeturn31view0turn18view1turn25view4

Third, dance is present but not always equally deep. Trinity integrates movement/dance into overall performance; LAMDA embeds physical response and staging; RSL publishes dance-specific technique points; LCME Diplomas is more holistic and less dance-call-specific than a conservatoire audition. Acceptd is strong on framing and “show your strengths” but has no mark bands. citeturn27view11turn20view1turn24view2turn18view1turn29view2

## Reusable Handoff Pack for MT-B3

### MT-B3 handoff summary

MT-B2 is complete for the visible batch. The strongest contribution of this batch is not more admissions-task detail, but formalised assessment language. LAMDA, Trinity, LCME and RSL all publish learning outcomes, mark bands, grading categories, or component/domain weightings that were largely missing from MT-B1 institutional admissions pages. The most useful sources for later calibration work are Trinity’s graded Musical Theatre syllabus, LCME Musical Theatre for Actors 2024, LCME Musical Theatre Diplomas 2025, and RSL/PAA Musical Theatre. These give the clearest public vocabulary for technical skill, interpretation, contextual understanding, communication, audience awareness, and reflection. citeturn31view0turn14view0turn18view1turn25view4

MT-B2 also clarifies structural distinctions inside the discipline. LAMDA Solo/Duo and Group are strongly acting-through-song frameworks; Trinity is fully integrated across solo, pair, group and production; LCME divides singer-led and actor-led routes at grade level before re-unifying them in the 2025 diploma; RSL is group-led but introduces an individual technical specialism; Acceptd provides a widely used prescreen standard but no adjudication model. citeturn26search0turn26search1turn31view0turn15search2turn15search3turn15search0turn25view1turn29view4

The remaining gap for MT-B3 is therefore practitioner judgement rather than exam-board structure: how casting professionals and high-authority industry bodies talk about self-tapes, recall value, what reads on camera, what makes material feel truthful rather than merely technically accomplished, and how they separate professional suitability from training descriptors. MT-B3 should not repeat exam-board mark bands. It should test where practitioner language agrees with, sharpens, or challenges the formal frameworks found here—especially around individuality, professional readiness, self-tape communication, and submission-level decision making.

### Open questions / limitations

This report completes the MT-B2 source set visible in the pasted handoff and public-source universe re-found from it. If an earlier private ledger contained additional MT-B2 rows that were not reproduced in the conversation, those rows were not visible for verification here. One narrow limitation remains within the completed extraction: LCME Singers’ detailed attainment-band prose was not sampled line-for-line in this run, although its component structure, assessment domains, and weightings were directly verified. Acceptd is included because the batch brief explicitly mentioned common prescreen standards; it is a common-standard comparator, not an exam-board award specification.# Musical Theatre Practitioner, Casting, Industry, and Self-Tape Guidance

## MT-B4 decision and reusable handoff pack

**Decision on MT-B4:** **MT-B4 is required.** MT-B3 materially strengthened authenticity, preparation, self-tape fairness, first-impression caution, and anti-bias boundaries, but it did not close the remaining subtype and pedagogy gaps: acting-through-song method, Golden Age versus contemporary handling, legit/belt/mix calibration, dance-led versus voice-led versus acting-led MT, and style-specific guidance for jukebox or through-composed material remain thin in MT-B1–MT-B3. Practitioner sources here are broad and process-heavy, not subtype-specific enough to finish synthesis safely. citeturn10view1turn35view2turn31view2

**MT-B4 handoff summary**

MT-B3 is now complete across all eleven repaired practitioner, casting, industry, and self-tape rows. Official guidance is strongest in **[MT-S055]** and **[MT-S056]**. [MT-S055] is the clearest formal source for fairness, accessibility, turnaround, cost burden, consent, and limits on what self-tape requests should ask of performers. [MT-S056] confirms the CDG’s public self-tape position and links to practitioner-facing resources on self-taping and MT auditions, including preparation, repertoire relevance, direction-response, and anti-bias boundaries around personal data. These two rows should shape later guardrails on what belongs in report structure, reliability language, and non-penalisation of access or resource constraints. citeturn19view1turn19view2turn30search0turn27view0turn10view1

The rest of MT-B3 is predominantly **practitioner opinion only**, not formal assessment design. **[MT-S057]**, **[MT-S058]**, **[MT-S059]**, **[MT-S061]**, **[MT-S064]**, and **[MT-S065]** add useful evidence on authenticity, preparation, clarity, flexibility, personhood, storytelling, reader use, and openness to direction. But they do not publish weightings or validated descriptors. Two Playbill video pages, **[MT-S062]** and **[MT-S063]**, remain low-descriptor: they verify broad topic areas but do not expose enough written substance to anchor detailed criteria. **[MT-S060]** is process-only platform guidance and should not be treated as evaluative evidence. citeturn26view0turn21view0turn23view0turn24view0turn35view0turn32view1turn33view0turn34view0turn25search0

MT-B3’s main value is **boundary-setting**: what can inform scoring only when observable, what belongs only in report language, and what must be excluded as bias-sensitive. MT-B4 is still needed because subtype/style questions remain unresolved: acting-through-song pedagogy, Golden Age versus contemporary, legit/belt/mix, dance-led vs voice-led vs acting-led MT, and other style-specific distinctions are not sufficiently covered by practitioner sources alone. citeturn10view1turn35view2turn31view2

**Self-tape/access/fairness findings to carry forward**

- Access needs should be asked and recorded for everyone, not inferred or waited for. [MT-S055] citeturn19view2  
- Technical polish beyond basic assessability should not become a proxy for talent. [MT-S055], [MT-S059] citeturn19view1turn23view0  
- Presentation/technical issues belong primarily in report structure and reliability language, unless they materially block assessment. [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S059] citeturn19view1turn28view0turn23view4  
- Platform workflow facts are operational, not evaluative. [MT-S060] citeturn25search0

**Bias-sensitive material to exclude**

- Body/type language, protected or personal data, identity proxies, nationality/passport cues, and age-appearance logistics. [MT-S056], [MT-S064] citeturn10view1turn35view4  
- Appearance-led or class-coded readings such as generic “well-presented” or dressing toward a role. [MT-S056], [MT-S058] citeturn28view1turn21view0  
- Social-media behaviour as a performance criterion. [MT-S063] citeturn34view0

**Gaps that MT-B4 should address**

- Acting-through-song pedagogy beyond generic authenticity language  
- Golden Age vs contemporary calibration  
- legit / belt / mix / pop-rock distinctions  
- dance-led vs voice-led vs acting-led MT  
- subtype distinctions such as jukebox and through-composed work  
- style-specific feedback language that is stronger than general practitioner advice

## Style and gap analysis

### MT subtype and style criteria table

| Subtype/style | Criteria supported by evidence | Shared criteria weighted differently | Shared criteria evidenced differently | Observable tape evidence required | What feedback must mention to be specific | What should be de-emphasised or excluded | Source ID(s) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dance-led MT | Musical risk-taking, musical use of the body, posture/technique/flexibility, choreography uptake, and story carried through movement. | Dance evidence should carry more explanatory weight than generic vocal praise. | Integration still matters, but movement command and physical storytelling are the clearest differentiators. | Full-body visibility, transition quality, rhythmic clarity, embodied character. | Named movement passage/combo, style cue, transition, and whether character survived the choreography. | Generic “great energy”; unsupported body comments. | [MT-S070], [MT-S074], [MT-S075] citeturn24view1turn24view4turn31view0turn33view0 | medium |
| Voice-led MT | Style-through-ages, Golden Age vs contemporary contrast, mix/belt/chest access, repertoire suitability, individuality/versatility. | Vocal-style evidence should carry more weight than dance polish if the material is voice-dominant. | Needs phrase/register/style evidence rather than global tone praise. | Register transition, text clarity, stylistic sound, 32-bar/full-song control where observable. | Exact phrase or register event, period/style, and how the sound served storytelling. | Tape-only vocal-health diagnosis; vague “strong voice”. | [MT-S072], [MT-S066], [MT-S067] citeturn26view0turn26view1turn27view0turn20view0turn20view1 | high |
| Acting-led MT | Actor-centred singing, speech-to-song continuity, objective through lyric, text/subtext, phrase-level choices, character ownership. | Acting evidence should carry more weight than vocal display if the source is actor-singer-led. | Truth of intention and lyric action matter more than vocal fireworks alone. | Spoken-sung continuity, beat change in lyric, relationship to imagined partner, purposeful phrasing. | Specific lyric or beat, action/objective, subtext, and whether phrasing/body language conveyed it. | Generic “emotional connection”; personality without evidence. | [MT-S067], [MT-S077], [MT-S079] citeturn20view1turn38search2turn38search1 | medium |
| Golden Age | Era-aware repertoire, appropriate sound aesthetics, interpretive and technical proficiency, stylistic distinction from contemporary MT. | Style clarity matters as much as raw vocal finish. | Often evidenced through diction, phrase shape, and period-appropriate vocal colour. | Period-appropriate phrasing, textual clarity, legato/line where relevant. | Why the performance read as Golden Age, not simply “classic” or “legit”. | Era labels without observable sound/text evidence. | [MT-S072], [MT-S074] citeturn26view0turn27view0turn31view0 | medium |
| Contemporary MT | Contemporary selections, mix/belt/chest access, style-appropriate sound, wide range across the modern canon. | Often needs more explicit comment on registration and vocal colour. | May rely more on speech-inflected phrasing, contemporary sound and register shifts. | Belt/mix access if clearly audible, contemporary diction/phrasing, not just “belt present”. | Specific section showing contemporary sound and how it served text. | Overclaiming “healthy belt” from tape alone. | [MT-S072], [MT-S077] citeturn26view0turn27view0turn38search2 | medium |
| Jukebox MT | Honour original style without imitation, familiar lyrics made character-driven, narrative integrity plus showmanship, choreography/ensemble momentum. | Source-song identity matters more here than in original-score MT, but imitation should not dominate. | Evidence lies in transformation of a familiar song into dramatic action. | Style authenticity, restraint from mimicry, ownership of lyric, integration with stage energy. | The known song/artist idiom, what the performer kept, what they transformed, and how character ownership emerged. | Karaoke comparison, celebrity impression standards. | [MT-S078] citeturn35search0turn37search2 | medium |
| Through-composed MT | Partial support only: continuity of intention, speech-to-song linkage, sustained character through extended singing. | Integration matters more than isolated “song moments”. | Evidence is continuous dramatic-musical flow, but no repaired MT-B4 source gives a dedicated rubric. | Transition continuity, sustained intention, stamina, no drop in character between sections. | Specific transition or extended passage, where intention held or dropped. | Treating this as fully solved by current evidence. | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] citeturn20view0turn31view0turn38search1 | low |

## Reusable handoff pack for MT-SYN

### MT-B4 completion summary

MT-B4 is complete. The repaired pack’s short-course, curriculum, junior-training, and coaching sources now all have final statuses, and three targeted gap-fill sources were added where the repaired pack alone was too thin: [MT-S077] for acting-through-song pedagogy, [MT-S078] for jukebox MT, and [MT-S079] for acting-led actor-singer work. The strongest MT-B4 evidence came from [MT-S072], which gives the clearest official public style-calibration language: one Golden Age selection, contemporary selections, mix/belt/chest access, individuality/versatility, and programme outcomes built around style-appropriate sound across the MT canon. [MT-S070] added unusually concrete dance/song/redirection/interview language, while [MT-S074] anchored Scene to Song, Golden Age, dance-form breadth and genre-appropriate interpretive/technical proficiency. [MT-S066], [MT-S067], [MT-S069] and [MT-S077] together materially strengthened acting-through-song beyond generic authenticity, pointing toward lyric intention, body language, phrasing, facial expression, speech-to-song continuity and story clarity. [MT-S078] closed the jukebox gap to a usable level by identifying style authenticity without imitation, character ownership of familiar lyrics, and the balance of narrative integrity with showmanship. citeturn26view0turn27view0turn24view1turn31view0turn20view0turn20view1turn22view8turn38search2turn35search0

The main unresolved subtype gap is **through-composed MT**. The current evidence supports only partial inference from acting-through-song, scene-to-song and actor-singer pedagogy; there is no dedicated through-composed/public rubric source in the repaired MT-B4 pack. MT-SYN should therefore treat through-composed criteria as an explicit evidence gap, not as a settled rule-set. More broadly, MT-B4’s evidence is strongest for **style/context language and observable-evidence requirements**, not for formal weightings. Short-course, curriculum and coaching sources must remain labelled as pedagogy/context rather than imported wholesale as admissions or scoring frameworks. [MT-S075] is useful only as coaching context, and [MT-S076] remains duplicate / superseded by MTCP/Acceptd. citeturn33view0turn32view0

### Strongest subtype/style/pedagogy findings

- **Acting-through-song** is now strongly evidenced as phrase-level dramatic work, not generic sincerity.
- **Golden Age vs contemporary** and **legit/mix/belt** distinctions are evidenced enough to support style-aware report language.
- **Jukebox MT** is now supported well enough for subtype-specific commentary.
- **Dance-led/voice-led/acting-led emphasis** is only partly resolved: there is enough evidence to justify different feedback emphases, but not strong evidence for fixed weighting rules.
- **Through-composed MT** remains the major unresolved subtype gap.

### Explicit caution for MT-SYN

MT-B4 is rich in **pedagogy, curriculum, short-course and coaching** material. It strengthens subtype-specific evidence requirements and report language, but it is **not** a substitute for formal assessment frameworks. MT-SYN should import from MT-B4 only where the source yields **observable performance evidence** or clear subtype-specific wording, and should explicitly preserve the distinction between **pedagogy/context** and **assessment criteria**.# Musical Theatre Synthesis

## Source-type comparison

| Source type | What it is strongest for | What it is weak for | How it should inform the rubric | What should not be imported directly | Representative Source ID(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Official institutions / admissions | Task structure, prescreen/recall requirements, training-potential language, public audition values, interview/process expectations | Formal weightings, mark bands, detailed adjudication descriptors | Core audition components, what evidence is expected, what “potential” means, what counts as course fit rather than role fit | Marketing copy, institution-specific logistics, programme-specific quirks as universal rules | MT-B1-002, MT-B1-005, MT-B1-006, MT-B1-009, MT-B1-023, MT-B1-030, [MT-S046], [MT-S050] |
| Exam boards / syllabi | Assessment domains, acting-through-song descriptors, technique vs interpretation vs communication, reflection/context, route logic, public weightings | Live professional casting pressures, self-tape fairness, admissions-panel judgement | Strong comparator for what should be evidenced and separated in comments; useful for category definitions and descriptor language | Exact exam percentages, discussion/reflection tasks, qualification-specific structures | [MT-S001], [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S007], [MT-S009] |
| Common prescreen standards | Submission comparability, timing, framing, option menus, file structure | Performance quality judgements, mark schemes, evaluator descriptors | Technical assessability and common component coverage | Any use as a scoring rubric | [MT-S011] |
| Practitioner / casting / industry guidance | Authenticity, preparation, direction-response, room expectations, first-impression cautions | Validated descriptors, weightings, bias control unless filtered, stable written detail in all cases | Filtered report language, cautionary boundaries, observable professionalism | Charm, taste, marketability, appearance-led or identity-led “fit” | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S061], [MT-S064], [MT-S065] |
| Self-tape fairness / access guidance | Non-penalisation, access/process fairness, cost burden, turnaround, consent, what assessors should not demand | Artistic scoring detail | Reliability language, fairness notes, non-penalisation guardrails | Any idea that low production value equals low talent | [MT-S055], [MT-S056] |
| Short-course / pedagogy / curriculum sources | Acting-through-song specificity, style/era language, subtype distinctions, observable detail for report wording | Formal scoring frameworks, universal admissions rules | Style-aware report wording, subtype evidence requirements, observable specificity | Course structures and pedagogy as direct scores or weightings | [MT-S066], [MT-S067], [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S077], [MT-S078], [MT-S079] |
| Coaching / secondary sources | Supporting context, novice-dancer or preparation cautions, subtype interpretation where official sources are thin | Neutrality, authority, formal criteria | Caution only; occasional report-language support where consistent with stronger sources | Direct criterion-setting, commercial claims, secondary reinterpretations of primary standards | [MT-S075], [MT-S076] |

## Core criteria and subtype synthesis

**Core Musical Theatre assessment criteria**

| Criterion | What it means in MT | Observable tape evidence | Source basis | Confidence | Scoring / report language / caution only / exclude |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting-through-song | Lyric intention, action/objective, phrase-level choices, speech-to-song continuity, relationship, subtext, dramatic use of phrasing | A specific lyric or phrase, beat change, partner focus, physical/facial shift, dramatic phrasing decision | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S066], [MT-S067], [MT-S077], [MT-S079], MT-B1-002, MT-B1-015, MT-B1-016 | High | **Scoring** |
| Vocal technique in service of story | Technique is not just pitch/control; it must support text, style and communication | Register changes, diction, line, breath management serving meaning, style-appropriate tone | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], MT-B1-020, MT-B1-017 | High | **Scoring** |
| Movement / dance in service of story | Movement is not generic “energy”; it includes musicality, physical storytelling, posture/control, transition clarity, response to choreography | Full-body evidence, rhythm, posture, clarity of movement choices, character through movement | MT-B1-006, [MT-S070], [MT-S074], [MT-S051] | Medium-High | **Scoring** |
| Integration of acting, singing and movement | MT-specific integration rather than three unrelated comments | Evidence that acting remains alive while singing/moving; no collapse into silos | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], MT-B1-008, MT-B1-030, [MT-S049], [MT-S074] | High | **Scoring**, but fixed separate weighting is not yet evidenced |
| Repertoire choice | Choice of piece(s) to suit style, era, voice, age/stage of development, and task brief | Contrast, suitability, style awareness, whether material overreaches or obscures strengths | MT-B1-002, MT-B1-015, MT-B1-016, [MT-S072], [MT-S064] | High | **Scoring — conditional on performer-controlled choice** |
| Lyric and text understanding | Understanding words, context, thought progression and dramatic function | Clear narrative through lyrics, precise thought changes, textual specificity | [MT-S001], [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S007], [MT-S077] | High | **Scoring** |
| Style / era / genre awareness | Golden Age vs contemporary vs jukebox etc are not interchangeable performance codes | Era-appropriate sound, phrasing, diction, stylistic restraint or idiomatic colour | [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S078], MT-B1-002, MT-B1-015 | Medium-High | **Scoring — conditional on identifiable style** |
| Preparation and readiness | Observable preparation, material ownership, reserve material readiness where context shows it | Secure starts/stops, ownership, clarity, callback readiness, compliance with task structure | MT-B1-023, [MT-S038], [MT-S044], [MT-S064], [MT-S058] | Medium-High | **Scoring — limited to observable preparation, not polish or privilege** |
| Individuality / authenticity | Not “charm”; specific, owned choices that do not feel imitative or generic | Distinctive but grounded interpretation, choice-making, text ownership | MT-B1-020, [MT-S046], [MT-S049], [MT-S057], [MT-S065] | Medium | **Scoring only when anchored to observable choices; otherwise report language** |
| Direction-response | Ability to absorb and apply notes or redirection when this is actually observable | Adjusted second take, callback/recall note response, live-choreography uptake | MT-B1-006, MT-B1-015, MT-B1-016, [MT-S070], [MT-S056], [MT-S065] | Medium | **Scoring — only if observable** |
| Self-tape assessability | Whether the tape is readable enough to support fair judgement | Audio clarity, framing, full-body visibility where needed, stable picture, file/readability | MT-B1-002, MT-B1-009, [MT-S011], [MT-S055], [MT-S059] | High | **Report language** |
| Professional-readiness signals | Relevant only when evidenced through preparation, communication and process-fit, not charisma | Reserve material, instructions followed, usable accompaniment, relevant slate/wildcard, calm process behaviour | MT-B1-005, MT-B1-017, MT-B1-023, [MT-S047], [MT-S054], [MT-S064] | Medium | **Report language** |
| Training potential vs casting suitability | Institutions often want potential, teachability and course fit rather than “perfect casting” | Evidence of promise, curiosity, adaptability, strongest current ability rather than ready-made type | MT-B1-005, [MT-S046], [MT-S047], [MT-S050], [MT-S054] | High | **Caution only as a design distinction; not a raw score** |

**Criteria by MT subtype / style**

| Subtype/style | Criteria supported by evidence | Shared criteria weighted differently | Shared criteria evidenced differently | Observable tape evidence required | Feedback must mention | What to de-emphasise or exclude | Source basis | Confidence | Evidence gap? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dance-led MT | Musical movement, choreography uptake, posture/control, risk-taking, physical storytelling | Dance and movement evidence should carry more explanatory weight than generic vocal praise | Integration still matters, but movement quality and embodied story are primary | Full body, transitions, timing, style-specific movement evidence, whether character survives movement | Named movement passage or combo, transition quality, style cue, embodied story | Body commentary; generic “good energy”; dance scored from cropped/partial evidence | MT-B1-006, [MT-S070], [MT-S051], [MT-S074], [MT-S075] | Medium | No, but weighting evidence remains limited |
| Voice-led MT | Style-through-ages, clarity of text, register choice, repertoire fit, versatility | Vocal-style evidence should dominate over dance polish where the material is voice-centred | More phrase/register/style detail is needed than in generic singing comments | Register shifts, diction, phrasing, style-appropriate vocal colour | Exact phrase/register event, period/style, how sound served text | Dance criticism when dance is not meaningfully present; tape-only vocal-health claims | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], MT-B1-020, MT-B1-017 | High | No |
| Acting-led MT | Objective through lyric, speech-song continuity, text/subtext, choice-making | Dramatic intention should outweigh vocal display if the piece is actor-singer-led | Evidence comes from lyric action and phrasing, not vocal fireworks alone | Beat change, action, imagined relationship, speech-like connection, phrase specificity | Lyric or beat, objective, subtext, response target | Generic “authentic” without textual evidence | [MT-S006], [MT-S067], [MT-S077], [MT-S079] | Medium | No |
| Golden Age | Era-aware repertoire, line, diction, stylistic restraint/shape, period-appropriate vocalism | Style clarity matters as much as generic vocal quality | Often evidenced through phrasing, diction and vocal colour rather than overt realism | Line, diction, phrasing, era-appropriate sound and textual interpretation | Why it reads as Golden Age rather than merely “classic” | Era labels without sound/text evidence | [MT-S072], [MT-S074], MT-B1-015, MT-B1-016 | Medium | No |
| Contemporary MT | Contemporary sound, speech-inflected phrasing, mix/belt where appropriate, current style handling | Contemporary style may require more explicit comment on register and colour | Evidence lies in present-day vocal idiom and lyric immediacy | Audible mix/belt or contemporary line, contemporary diction, style handling | Specific phrase showing contemporary sound and dramatic function | Generic “modern” or “current” labels | [MT-S072], MT-B1-002, MT-B1-020 | Medium | Partial |
| Jukebox MT | Style authenticity without imitation, ownership of familiar lyrics, narrative integrity with showmanship | Familiar-song management matters more than in original-score MT | Evidence lies in transformation of a known song into character action | Retention of idiom without mimicry; dramatic ownership of familiar lyric | Source-song idiom, what was transformed, how character took ownership | Karaoke comparison; celebrity imitation standards | [MT-S078] | Medium | No |
| Through-composed MT | Continuity of intention, sustained character, transition discipline, stamina | Integration matters more than isolated “song moments” | Evidence should come from extended sung continuity rather than separate songs | Sustained intention through transitions, no drop in dramatic line, emotional/technical stamina | Specific transition or extended passage where character/intention held or dropped | Treating it as fully solved by existing evidence | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Low | **Yes** |
| Legit / mix / belt / pop-rock | Register choice, style authenticity, diction, sound colour, idiomatic handling | Style-specific vocal evidence should shift emphasis inside a shared vocal area | Legit often needs line/diction; mix/belt needs register/colour evidence; pop-rock needs idiom without imitation | Register evidence, style-appropriate sound, text clarity | Style label plus audible evidence | Medical/fach claims from tape | [MT-S072], [MT-S078], MT-B1-002 | Medium | Partial |
| Acting-through-song | Lyric intention, body/facial expression, character journey, phrase-level dramatic work | Often should outweigh generic “good singing” language in MT | Evidence is in phrasing, body response, target, dramatic arc | Lyric beat, gesture, focus shift, phrase intention | Phrase/lyric, target, action, dramatic use of musical phrasing | Generic “good storytelling” without lyric evidence | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S066], [MT-S067], [MT-S069], [MT-S077], [MT-S079] | High | No |

## Scoring and report implications

**Scoring implications**

Do not read these as final rubric wording. They are audit-level design implications only.

| Scoring area | Why it matters in MT | Suggested design implication | Source ID(s) | Confidence | Caution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting | MT still requires acting, but often through lyric and sung text rather than spoken scene alone | Audit whether acting language in MT explicitly captures **acting-through-song**, not just generic “connection” | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077], MT-B1-002, MT-B1-023, MT-B1-030 | High | Do not assume spoken-scene evidence exists in a song-only tape |
| Voice / singing | Voice must be judged in relation to style, text, and communication, not only pitch/range | Audit whether vocal scoring requires **style-aware evidence** and **story-serving technique**, not generic vocal praise | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], MT-B1-020, MT-B1-017 | High | Do not turn tape impressions into vocal-health diagnosis |
| Dance / movement | MT dance evidence is distinct from generic “movement” enthusiasm | Audit whether movement scoring is used only when **visible and assessable**, with movement-story evidence required | MT-B1-006, [MT-S070], [MT-S051], [MT-S074] | Medium-High | Defer exact movement weighting to later Dance research |
| Integration | MT specificity depends heavily on integration across acting, singing and movement | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting.** Audit whether integration must be evidenced in report text even if not a separate numeric field | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], MT-B1-008, MT-B1-030, [MT-S049] | High | Strong evidence for explicit reporting; weaker for a mandatory standalone score |
| Repertoire / style fit | Repertoire can reveal judgement, suitability and style awareness | Audit whether repertoire choice is scored **only when performer-controlled** or brief-relevant; otherwise keep in report language | MT-B1-002, MT-B1-015, MT-B1-016, [MT-S072], [MT-S064] | High | Fixed-material tasks should not be penalised as if choice were free |
| Direction-response | Casting and some institutional sources treat this as important | Audit whether direction-response can be scored **only where observable** (callback, redo, recall, redirection), otherwise omitted from scoring | MT-B1-006, MT-B1-015, [MT-S070], [MT-S056], [MT-S065] | Medium | Do not infer it from a single finished tape |
| Self-tape assessability | A tape can be technically imperfect yet still fair to assess | Keep assessability in technical/reliability/report structure, **not as a standalone artistic score** | MT-B1-002, MT-B1-009, [MT-S011], [MT-S055], [MT-S059] | High | Penalise only where assessability is materially affected |
| Fairness / access | These are boundaries on evaluation, not performance dimensions | Keep access and fairness in reliability/report notes and guardrails, **not in scoring** | [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | High | Non-penalisation is the design implication |
| Professional readiness | Institutions and practitioners value preparation and readiness, but this can slide into class/taste bias | Keep most professional-readiness signals in report language or verdict rationale, not as a standalone score | MT-B1-005, MT-B1-023, [MT-S047], [MT-S054], [MT-S064] | Medium | Avoid vague polish/charm scoring |
| Exam-board percentages | Exam boards publish useful weightings internally | **Do not import exact exam-board percentages directly.** Use them only as design comparators for domain separation | [MT-S006], [MT-S007], [MT-S009] | High | Those frameworks are educational and qualification-specific |
| Dance-led / voice-led / acting-led emphasis | Evidence supports subtype-sensitive emphasis shifts | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting.** Defer any design-level weighting decision to later Dance, Acting, and Voice/Singing research | [MT-S051], [MT-S070], [MT-S072], [MT-S075], [MT-S079] | Medium | This is the clearest remaining weighting gap |

**Report-structure implications**

| Report section or feedback area | What it should require | Observable evidence required | Source basis | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Material-specific comments | Name the actual song/scene/material function where possible | Lyric, phrase, beat, dance combo, moment, or component | MT-B1-002, MT-B1-015, MT-B1-016, [MT-S077], [MT-S078] | High |
| Style/subtype-specific comments | Identify the MT style or subtype if observable and relevant | Era/style cue, register, idiom, repertoire type, source-song handling | [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S078] | Medium-High |
| Performer-specific choices | Tie praise/critique to a choice this performer made | Specific action, phrasing choice, relationship, movement choice | [MT-S006], [MT-S065], MT-B1-023 | High |
| Acting-through-song evidence | Require lyric or phrase evidence; do not allow generic “good storytelling” | Lyric intention, body language, phrase turn, target, subtext | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | High |
| Vocal-style evidence | Require style-aware vocal evidence, not just “strong voice” | Register change, diction, line, style-appropriate sound | [MT-S007], [MT-S072] | High |
| Movement / dance evidence | Require visible movement evidence when dance is commented on | Full-body moment, transition, choreography uptake, musical use of body | MT-B1-006, [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | Medium-High |
| Integration evidence | Require explicit comment on how acting, singing and movement interact | Same moment showing more than one discipline working together | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], MT-B1-030, [MT-S049] | High |
| Self-tape assessability / reliability note | Separate reliability from quality | What was or was not assessable due to sound/framing/visibility | [MT-S011], [MT-S055], [MT-S059] | High |
| Fairness/access note | Where relevant, note that adjustments or technical limits should not be misread as weakness | Clear access context or fairness limitation | [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | High |
| Excluded/non-penalised technical limitations | Make explicit what was not penalised | Low production value, reader limitations, basic home setup, short turnaround | [MT-S055], [MT-S059], [MT-S060] | High |

## Risks, exclusions and evidence gaps

**Generic feedback risks**

| Generic feedback risk | Why it is generic in MT | What observable evidence must replace it | Source basis | Example of the evidence the report must reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| “Great stage presence” | Can mean charm, charisma, type, volume, or simple confidence; it is too vague and bias-prone | What the performer actually did to hold focus: lyric ownership, target, movement clarity, phrase control | [MT-S065], [MT-S058], MT-B1-023 | A specific lyric or transition where attention was held because intention stayed precise |
| “Strong voice” | Says nothing about style, story, diction, or how voice served the material | Register event, style handling, diction, line, dynamic or phrase choice | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], MT-B1-020 | A belt/mix moment or Golden Age phrase that clarified text and style |
| “Good storytelling” | Could apply to any decent performance without proving MT specificity | Lyric beat, objective, partner relationship, phrase turn, song-to-scene continuity | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | The line or lyric where the action changed and the intention became clearer |
| “Nice movement” | Too broad; could mean energy, rhythm, fitness, or just motion | Posture/control, transition, choreography uptake, body used musically, character maintained | MT-B1-006, [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | The dance phrase or movement transition that conveyed story or responded cleanly to style |
| “Authentic performance” | Often collapses into taste or personality judgement | Concrete choices that felt owned rather than imitative; clear relation to text | [MT-S057], [MT-S065], [MT-S073] | A choice in delivery that felt specific to this performer and material rather than generic |
| “Professional tape” | Can become a proxy for money or equipment | Only comment on what materially helped or hindered assessability | [MT-S055], [MT-S059], [MT-S011] | Whether sound/framing let acting, dancing or lyrics be read clearly |
| “Good energy” | Common but empty; may drift into personality bias | Musical drive, physical commitment, pace through choreography, clear intention | [MT-S070], [MT-S061] | A movement passage or lyric section where energy had a specific dramatic function |

**Exclusions and anti-bias guardrails**

| Excluded or cautious area | Why it must not become a scoring criterion | Safer handling | Source ID(s) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Body / type / appearance | Bias-sensitive and unrelated to talent or process fairness | Exclude completely from scoring and feedback unless a safety/access issue directly affects assessability | [MT-S056], [MT-S064] | High |
| Protected characteristics | Identity data must not proxy for skill | Exclude from scoring; do not solicit or reward | [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | High |
| Nationality / passport / identity data | Administrative or identity information is not artistic evidence | Exclude from performer scoring; keep only as external process data if ever needed operationally | [MT-S056] | High |
| Class-coded presentation | “Well-presented” can drift into class or expense bias | Reframe only in terms of assessability and distraction, not polish or taste | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S059] | High |
| Vague charisma / charm / “presence” | Too subjective unless anchored to evidence | Use only when tied to specific observable choices; otherwise exclude | [MT-S058], [MT-S061], [MT-S064], [MT-S065] | Medium |
| Social-media behaviour | Not a performance criterion | Exclude from scoring | [MT-S063] | High |
| Expensive tape production | Resource-heavy production is not talent | Score only assessability, not polish beyond that threshold | [MT-S055], [MT-S059] | High |
| Access needs | Adjustments are not weakness | Note in fairness/reliability language; do not penalise | [MT-S055] | High |

## Final reusable MT-SYN handoff pack for MT-AUDIT

**MT synthesis summary**

Musical Theatre research is complete across admissions/institutional evidence, exam-board frameworks, practitioner/industry guidance, and subtype/style pedagogy. The strongest **official admissions** sources are MT-B1-002, MT-B1-005, MT-B1-006, MT-B1-009, MT-B1-020, MT-B1-023, MT-B1-030, [MT-S046], [MT-S047], [MT-S049], [MT-S050], [MT-S051] and [MT-S054]. Together they establish the public shape of MT auditions: contrasting repertoire, acting-through-song, dance or movement assessability, individuality/personhood components, callback or recall expansion, interview/process signals, and a recurring distinction between **training potential** and **ready-made casting fit**. Penn State’s “professional potential” versus “perfect casting decision” language is especially important for that separation. MT-B1-002 MT-B1-005 MT-B1-006 MT-B1-009 MT-B1-020 MT-B1-023 MT-B1-030 [MT-S046] [MT-S049] [MT-S050] [MT-S051] [MT-S054]

The strongest **exam-board** sources are [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S007] and [MT-S009]. These give the clearest public descriptor language for MT as an integrated discipline: acting, singing and movement together; lyric connection; interpretation distinct from technical accomplishment; knowledge/understanding distinct from communication; and, in RSL, a clear split between performance, technique and reflection. LCME is especially valuable because it explicitly separates **actor-led** and **singer-led** MT routes. That supports route-sensitive wording and evidence requirements, but not automatic route-specific numeric weighting. [MT-S004] [MT-S005] [MT-S006] [MT-S007] [MT-S009]

The strongest **practitioner and industry** sources are [MT-S055] and [MT-S056] for fairness, access, turnaround, technical burden, direction-response and anti-bias boundaries. Practitioner-opinion sources [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S061], [MT-S064] and [MT-S065] add authenticity, preparation, ownership, flexibility and lyric-storytelling emphasis, but they must be filtered carefully: only observable behaviour should influence scoring, while taste-based or bias-sensitive material must stay out. [MT-S055] [MT-S056] [MT-S057] [MT-S058] [MT-S061] [MT-S064] [MT-S065]

The strongest **subtype/style** sources are [MT-S070], [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S077], [MT-S078] and [MT-S079]. These close the acting-through-song gap and materially improve style calibration for Golden Age versus contemporary material, legit/mix/belt handling, dance-led versus actor-/voice-led emphasis, and jukebox MT. They are strong enough to support **style-aware report language** and **observable evidence requirements**, but not to justify fixed subtype weightings. Through-composed MT remains only partly supported and must stay an explicit evidence gap. [MT-S070] [MT-S072] [MT-S074] [MT-S077] [MT-S078] [MT-S079]

**Key evidence findings mapped to source IDs**

- **Acting-through-song must be evidenced, not implied:** [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077]  
- **Voice must be judged in service of story and style:** [MT-S007], [MT-S072], MT-B1-020  
- **Dance notes need visible, story-linked movement evidence:** MT-B1-006, [MT-S070], [MT-S051]  
- **Integration is core to MT and needs explicit report treatment:** [MT-S004], [MT-S009], MT-B1-030, [MT-S049]  
- **Self-tape fairness and access must shape reliability language:** [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011]  
- **Jukebox MT and style/era distinctions need subtype-aware language:** [MT-S072], [MT-S078], [MT-S074]  
- **Through-composed MT remains a real gap:** [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079]

**Audit priorities**

1. Force lyric/phrase evidence in MT feedback.  
2. Separate vocal technique from communication/story.  
3. Require visible movement evidence before commenting on dance.  
4. Separate assessability/fairness from performance quality.  
5. Capture subtype/style where observable.  
6. Filter practitioner opinion for bias and observability.  
7. Treat through-composed MT as an explicit evidence gap.  
8. Defer fixed subtype weighting changes to later Dance, Acting, and Voice/Singing research.# Musical Theatre Rubric Gap Audit
