| [MT-S079] | Italia Conti Acting (Musical Theatre) intensive | Official short-course pedagogy | https://www.italiaconti.com/product/acting-musical-theatre-2-week-intensive | MT-B4 | pedagogy/context source only | Acting-led MT / actor-singer work | Medium |
| [MT-S066] | RADA Musical Theatre short course | Official short-course pedagogy | https://www.rada.ac.uk/short-courses/musical-theatre/ | MT-B4 | pedagogy/context source only | Partial support for through-composed continuity and integrated storytelling | Medium |

**Source-Type Comparison**

| Source type | What it is strongest for | What it is weak for | How it should inform the rubric | What should not be imported directly | Representative Source ID(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Official institutions / admissions | Public audition tasks, component structure, training-potential language, personhood/interview elements, what schools ask candidates to show | Fixed universal scoring bands, universally transferable weighting | Inform category emphasis, component expectations, and report requirements | Fixed weights, universal role-fit logic, or institution-specific process rules | [MT-S013], [MT-S018], [MT-S019], [MT-S037], [MT-S045], [MT-S046], [MT-S049] |
| Exam boards / syllabi | Assessment domains, acting-through-song, technique vs interpretation vs communication, integrated MT logic | Conservatoire-specific casting fit, self-tape workflow, professional market realities | Inform evidence requirements and category distinctions inside existing fields | Exact percentages, formal reflection tasks, qualification structures | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S007], [MT-S009] |
| Common prescreen standards | Submission comparability, timing, framing, component coverage, assessability | Performance quality scoring, descriptor language, weighting | Inform report structure and reliability/assessability handling | Any use as a grading rubric | [MT-S011] |
| Practitioner / casting / industry guidance | Authenticity, preparation, individuality, first-impression caution, direction-response, professional conduct | Validated scoring anchors, consistent thresholds, anti-bias consistency unless filtered | Inform report language and conditional evidence rules | Taste, charm, marketability, appearance, social-media logic | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S061], [MT-S064], [MT-S065] |
| Self-tape fairness / access guidance | Non-penalisation, technical burden, access, turnaround, unsafe request limits | Performance-quality descriptors | Inform reliability language, fairness notes, technical/presentation handling | Production value as talent, access needs as weakness | [MT-S055], [MT-S056] |
| Short-course / pedagogy / curriculum sources | Style-specific wording, subtype distinctions, acting-through-song specificity, genre calibration | Formal assessment bands, universal admissions criteria | Inform observable-evidence requirements and subtype-aware commentary | Formal scoring rules, weightings, admissions-rubric logic | [MT-S066], [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S077], [MT-S078], [MT-S079] |
| Coaching / secondary sources | Context, caution, practical framing | Formal criteria-setting | Support weak patterns already anchored elsewhere | Independent criterion-setting or score logic | [MT-S075], [MT-S076] |

## Current Strengths

**Already Covered Well**

| Rubric area | What is already covered | Why it is credible / useful | Source basis from MT-SYN | Baseline impact | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting and vocal both central in MT | Run 0B keeps acting and vocal as the two central MT score areas, each at 30% | Official admissions and exam-board evidence repeatedly treat MT as centred on acting plus singing, even when integrated with movement | [MT-S004], [MT-S007], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | Preserve | High |
| Multi-component MT logic | Run 0B explicitly treats MT as usually acting scene + song, with component breakdown as important | This matches public audition structures and the strongest stabilised MT flow in the baseline | [MT-S013], [MT-S034], [MT-S045], [MT-S049], [MT-S011] | Preserve | High |
| Acting-through-song is at least recognised | Run 0B already states vocal must not be treated only as technical singing and that song feedback should cover lyric intention and acting through song | This aligns with the strongest MT-SYN evidence and means the rubric is already pointed in the right direction | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Improve | High |
| Transition awareness | Run 0B already says specificity should distinguish spoken scene work, sung work, and transition between scene and song | This is genuinely MT-specific and should not regress into separate-silo comments | [MT-S004], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | Preserve | High |
| Timestamp spread across components | Run 0B says timestamps should cover acting and song where possible | This matches the evidence requirement for multi-component MT assessability and the 0E MT guardrail | [MT-S013], [MT-S011], [MT-S049] | Preserve | High |
| Existing report scaffold | Component breakdown, category breakdown, strengths, improvements, fix-first, timestamps and next-take plan are already named | Those sections can carry much stronger MT evidence without changing the score schema | [MT-S037], [MT-S045], [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | Preserve | High |
| Role fit conditional on brief | Run 0B keeps role fit where brief exists rather than as a universal score driver | This is compatible with the MT-SYN distinction between training potential and narrow casting match | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S037] | Preserve | High |
| Known MT gaps are explicitly acknowledged | Run 0B already notes that acting-through-song is not fully formalised and that MT subtypes are not separately captured | This is accurate against the synthesis and helps prevent false claims of completeness | [MT-S072], [MT-S078], [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Preserve | High |
| No new MT score fields are assumed | Run 0B stays within the six-field operational system | This is compatible with the baseline do-not-touch list and with the evidence, which supports stronger wording more than new scoring fields | [MT-S004], [MT-S007], [MT-S009] | Preserve | High |

## Gaps and Risks

**Missing or Underdeveloped**

| Rubric area | Missing or underdeveloped issue | Why it matters in MT | Observable tape evidence that should be required | MT subtype/style affected | Source basis from MT-SYN | Evidence strength | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting-through-song | Recognised but not structurally guaranteed | MT-specific storytelling often happens inside the song, not beside it | Lyric beat, phrase change, objective/action, imagined relationship, body/focus shift | All MT; especially acting-led MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Strong | High |
| Song storytelling evidence | No explicit requirement to cite lyric / phrase / beat evidence | Without it, “good storytelling” remains generic and non-specific | Exact lyric moment, phrase, dynamic or breath choice tied to story shift | All MT; especially acting-led and contemporary MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Strong | High |
| Vocal evaluation | Technique and communication/story are not explicitly separated inside the vocal area | MT-SYN shows these are related but not identical | Register choice, diction, style, tone/placement, and whether they supported the lyric/story | Voice-led MT; Golden Age; contemporary; legit/mix/belt | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | Strong | High |
| Movement / dance evidence | Movement can still be commented on generically | MT dance notes need visible, story-linked evidence rather than “nice movement” | Full-body movement moment, rhythm change, posture, risk-taking, transition, character through movement | Dance-led MT; integrated MT | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | Strong | High |
| Integration | Component breakdown exists, but integration is not clearly required as an evidence category | MT should not read like separate acting and singing reports pasted together | Scene-to-song transition, acting continuity in song, movement-as-story, component interplay | All MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | Strong | High |
| Style / subtype specificity | MT subtypes are acknowledged as gaps, but the rubric does not yet force observable subtype handling | Style and era affect what counts as strong evidence | Era/style cue, register, diction, dance vocabulary, non-imitative jukebox handling | Golden Age, contemporary, legit/mix/belt, jukebox | [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S078] | Moderate | High |
| Self-tape assessability vs performance quality | The slice does not explicitly separate assessability/reliability from quality judgment | Low-budget or access-adapted tapes risk being penalised if not separated | Basic audibility, framing, visibility of movement, accompaniment balance, whether evidence is judgeable | All MT; especially self-taped song and dance | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | Strong | High |
| Training potential vs casting suitability | Not explicitly bounded inside the rubric slice | MT institutions often look for potential, not “perfect casting,” and role-fit logic can become unsafe if unbounded | Observable readiness, responsiveness if visible, strengths-led material handling, not market type | All MT; especially foundation/vocational and pre-professional | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S054] | Strong | High |
| Direction-response | Not explicitly conditional on observability | Many MT tapes do not show notes/redirection; scoring it anyway would be invented | Only score/report if an alternate take, note application, or live redirect is actually visible | Recall/workshop/room-based material mainly | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S070] | Moderate | High |
| Through-composed MT | Not surfaced as an evidence gap | The subtype remains only partly supported and must not be treated as solved | Continuous sung intention, transition continuity, stamina, no character drop across sections | Through-composed / sung-through | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Gap | High |
| Individuality / authenticity | Still vulnerable to generic or taste-based language | Practitioner evidence supports it, but only if tied to observable choices | Distinct choice, non-imitation, ownership of lyric/text, person-to-camera response if present | All MT, especially jukebox and callbacks | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S078] | Moderate | Medium |
| Professional-readiness signals | Can drift into generic polish or “commercially suitable” language | Professionalism must be observable and bounded, not charm- or polish-based | File discipline, accompanist readiness, prepared cuts, clear instructions followed, interview behaviour if visible | All MT | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S064] | Moderate | Medium |

**Generic-Feedback Risks**

Benchmark question: *Could this feedback only have been written about this specific MT tape, performer, material, style/subtype, and observable evidence?*

| Generic risk | Where it appears in the rubric | Why it is too generic for MT | What observable evidence must replace it | Source basis from MT-SYN | Recommended audit action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| “Great stage presence” | Acting / headline / strengths | Can mean charisma, bias, or general confidence rather than evidence | Name the exact stillness, focus, movement, entrance, or lyric-moment choice that made the performer readable | [MT-S058], [MT-S064], [MT-S070] | Replace with behaviour-anchored evidence | High |
| “Strong voice” | Vocal / strengths | Says nothing about style, story, or musical function | Cite register, era/style, phrase, diction, sustain, transition, and whether it served character/story | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | Require style-and-story vocal evidence | High |
| “Good storytelling” | Acting / vocal / overview | MT storytelling often lives inside lyric, phrasing, and transition, not just broad emotion | Cite lyric-beat, objective/action, phrase shape, focus shift, or scene-to-song continuity | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Require lyric/phrase evidence | High |
| “Nice movement” | Acting / technical / strengths | Generic movement praise ignores visibility, style, and dramatic function | Cite visible full-body moment, rhythm change, physical dynamic, posture/technique, or character through movement | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | Require visible movement evidence | High |
| “Authentic performance” | Acting / overview / strengths | Can become taste-based unless anchored to choices | Cite non-imitation, own accent/voice where relevant, material ownership, or specific choice-making | [MT-S057], [MT-S065], [MT-S073] | Keep only with observed choice evidence | High |
| “Professional tape” | Technical / presentation | Risks rewarding budget or polish rather than assessability | Cite audibility, stable framing, readable lighting, accompaniment balance, file/order clarity | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | Limit to assessability and reliability | High |
| “Good energy” | Acting / movement / headline | Too vague and often transferable across tapes | Cite tempo, attack, commitment, choreographic intention, breath impulse, or scene-to-song lift | [MT-S070], [MT-S078], [MT-S079] | Replace with moment-specific energy evidence | Medium |
| “Good connection” | Acting / vocal | Connection to what: reader, lyric, imagined partner, camera, audience? | Cite relationship target, eye-line, lyric address, or specific listening/response moment | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S045] | Force relationship target in feedback | High |
| “Clear potential” | Verdict / role fit / strengths | Can become unbounded optimism or appearance-based fit | Cite specific trainable strengths, strongest-skill presentation, or observable readiness markers | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S054] | Bound potential to observable evidence | High |
| “Commercially suitable” | Role fit / professional_presentation | Risks marketability and appearance bias | Reframe only as material/style/context fit where a brief explicitly supports it | [MT-S046], [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | Suppress unless brief-bounded and evidence-based | High |
| “Polished performance” | Overview / professional_presentation | Can reward coaching or production polish rather than MT skill | Cite preparation markers: secure cuts, score prep, clarity under self-tape conditions, visible control of material | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S064] | Reframe as observable preparation | Medium |

**MT Regression Risks**

| Regression risk | Affected rubric / baseline area | Why it is a risk | Source or guardrail basis | Safer handling | Baseline impact | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Changing MT weights or acting/vocal centrality | MT weights, acting + vocal visibility | MT is the protected regression anchor and the evidence supports central acting/vocal treatment, not a new weighting model | Run 0B slice; 0E MT stabilisation guardrails; [MT-S004], [MT-S007] | Preserve current weights and visible acting/vocal categories | Preserve | High |
| Removing component breakdown or weakening component spread | Component breakdown / timestamp spread | Would break the strongest stabilised MT flow and hide scene/song structure | 0E guardrail pack; [MT-S013], [MT-S045], [MT-S049], [MT-S011] | Preserve component breakdown and require stronger evidence inside it | Preserve | High |
| Importing exact exam-board percentages | Scoring logic | Exam-board percentages are educational design comparators, not conservatoire-audition weights | [MT-S007], [MT-S009]; 0E scoring guardrails | Use only as comparator; do not import directly | Defer | High |
| Adding a new acting-through-song score field | Schema / score fields | Baseline forbids new score fields without explicit approval, and evidence does not require a new field to strengthen specificity | 0E do-not-touch list; [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Improve evidence requirements within existing acting/vocal structure | Preserve | High |
| Scoring direction-response when not visible | Acting / professional_presentation | Most tapes do not show redirectability, so scoring it universally would invent evidence | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S070] | Suppress conditionally unless observable | Suppress conditionally | High |
| Penalising low-budget, adapted, or access-led tapes | Technical / audio / presentation | Fairness guidance explicitly warns against production-value bias and access penalties | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011]; 0E fairness guardrails | Separate assessability from quality; use reliability note | Preserve | High |
| Treating pedagogy as formal scoring rules | Subtype/style calibration | MT-B4 sources are valuable but mostly pedagogy/context only | [MT-S066], [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S077], [MT-S078] | Use for report language and evidence specificity, not fixed scoring rules | Preserve | High |
| Treating through-composed MT as solved | Subtype logic | The synthesis explicitly says it remains partly unresolved | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Keep visible as evidence gap and defer rule-making | Defer | High |
| Turning practitioner taste into rubric criteria | Acting / professional_presentation / role fit | Practitioner sources are useful only where filtered for observability and bias | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S064], [MT-S065]; 0E anti-bias guardrails | Keep as report language or caution unless observable | Suppress conditionally | High |
| Requiring backend or schema changes to capture subtype | Do-not-touch list | Outside audit scope and baseline-protected | 0E do-not-touch list | Audit wording/evidence rules only; no pipeline recommendation | Defer | High |

## Criteria and Design Implications

**Core Musical Theatre Assessment Criteria**

| Criterion | What it means in MT | Observable tape evidence | Source basis | Confidence | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting-through-song | Dramatic action, relationship, intention, and story carried through lyrics and music | Lyric beat, phrase emphasis, action/objective shift, focus change, body/facial expression, speech-to-song continuity | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | High | Scoring |
| Vocal technique in service of story | Technique matters, but not as an isolated sound contest | Diction, phrasing, register, breath/line, tone placement, style-appropriate sound, and whether those served the lyric | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | High | Scoring |
| Movement / dance in service of story | Movement is not just energy; it must be readable and often narrative | Full-body visibility, rhythm, posture, risk-taking, choreographic clarity, character through movement | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | High | Scoring when observable |
| Integration of acting, singing, and movement | MT is an integrated form, not three siloed disciplines | Scene-to-song continuity, movement that supports lyrics, acting that survives music, component interplay | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | High | Scoring + report language |
| Repertoire choice | Material choice can reveal judgment, style awareness, and suitability to the task | Contrast, era/style fit, age/context suitability, avoidance of imitation where relevant | [MT-S013], [MT-S034], [MT-S072], [MT-S078] | High | Scoring when performer-controlled; otherwise report language |
| Lyric and text understanding | MT performance should show understanding of what is being said and why | Clear sense of meaning, objective, subtext, given circumstances, phrase logic | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S007] | High | Scoring |
| Style / era / genre awareness | Golden Age, contemporary, legit/mix/belt, jukebox and related styles need different evidence | Era-appropriate phrasing, stylistic sound, non-imitation, genre-aware interpretation | [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S078] | Moderate | Scoring when observable |
| Preparation and readiness | Prepared cuts, correct task handling, file discipline, score/pianist readiness, clear following of task instructions | Secure cuts, clear slate/order, appropriate accompaniment, visible prep choices, reserve material only if visible/mentioned | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S064], [MT-S013] | Moderate | Scoring + report language |
| Individuality / authenticity | Not generic charm; evidence of ownership and non-imitation | Distinct choice-making, own vocal/personhood imprint, clear material ownership | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S078] | Moderate | Report language unless tied to clear choices |
| Direction-response | Only relevant if actual adjustment or redirectability is visible | Alternate take, visible note application, documented live redirect, or explicit response moment | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S070] | Moderate | Scoring only if observable |
| Self-tape assessability | Whether the tape is clear enough to judge fairly | Audibility, framing, full-body visibility where needed, accompaniment balance, readable technical setup | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | High | Report language |
| Professional-readiness signals | Observable signs of organised, audition-ready practice | Clear file discipline, accompanist communication, prepared materials, appropriate live/recall readiness | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S064] | Moderate | Report language |
| Training potential vs casting suitability | Institutions often separate trainability from narrow role/casting match | Strengths-led task handling, readiness markers, curiosity/promise if observable; not marketability or look | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S054] | High | Caution only / report language |

**Criteria by MT Subtype / Style**

| Subtype/style | Criteria supported by evidence | Shared criteria weighted differently | Shared criteria evidenced differently | Observable tape evidence required | Feedback must mention | What to de-emphasise or exclude | Source basis | Confidence | Evidence gap? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dance-led MT | Musical use of the body, posture, flexibility, risk-taking, choreography uptake, movement-led storytelling | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting** | Story may be carried more through movement transitions and physical attack than through vocal detail alone | Full-body movement, transition quality, rhythmic clarity, embodied character | The actual combo/passage, the movement vocabulary, and how story survived the dance | Generic “good energy”; body comments; hidden/partial-body claims | [MT-S070], [MT-S074], [MT-S051] | Moderate | No, but weighting remains a gap |
| Voice-led MT | Style-through-ages, Golden Age vs contemporary handling, mix/belt/chest access, vocal colour, versatility | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting** | Evidence sits more in register, line, diction, style, phrasing and tonal choices | Register event, style cue, phrase, diction choice, 32-bar/full-song handling if present | Phrase, register, style/era, and how voice served lyric/story | Tape-only vocal-health claims; vague “strong voice” | [MT-S072], [MT-S007], [MT-S034] | High | No, but weighting remains a gap |
| Acting-led MT | Actor-centred singing, objective through lyric, speech-to-song continuity, phrase-level acting | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting** | Evidence lies in action, subtext, relationship target, and lyric-driven choice-making | Spoken-sung continuity, beat shift, target/relationship, dramatic phrasing | Lyric/beat, objective, relationship, and dramatic use of phrasing | Generic “emotional connection” without lyric evidence | [MT-S006], [MT-S067], [MT-S077], [MT-S079] | Moderate | No, but weighting remains a gap |
| Golden Age | Era-aware repertoire, appropriate sound aesthetics, interpretive and technical style distinction | Style clarity may matter as much as raw vocal finish | More likely to require line, diction, phrase shape, period-aware sound | Period-appropriate phrase shape, diction, line, era-specific handling | Why the performance read as Golden Age, not just “classic” | Era labels without sound/text evidence | [MT-S072], [MT-S074] | Moderate | No |
| Contemporary MT | Contemporary sound, speech-inflected phrasing where appropriate, mix/belt/chest access, modern canon awareness | Style evidence often needs explicit weight in feedback | More likely to be heard in register shifts, diction, attack/release, colour | Specific contemporary phrase, register, sound, text clarity | Where contemporary sound appeared and how it served the material | Overclaiming health or style mastery from one phrase | [MT-S072], [MT-S077] | Moderate | Partly |
| Jukebox MT | Style authenticity without imitation, familiar lyric ownership, balance of showmanship and narrative integrity | Ownership and non-imitation deserve more emphasis than novelty of material | Evidence depends on transforming a known song into character action | Style authenticity, non-imitation, lyric ownership, controlled showmanship | The known style source, what was retained, what was transformed | Karaoke comparisons; celebrity imitation standards | [MT-S078] | Moderate | No |
| Through-composed MT | Continuity of intention, character, and musical-dramatic transitions across extended sung material | Integration matters more than isolated song moments | Evidence sits in sustained continuity rather than neat “song breaks” | Transition continuity, stamina, sustained character, no drop in intention | The extended passage or transition where continuity held or dropped | Pretending a full rule set exists | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Low | **Yes** |
| Legit / mix / belt / pop-rock | Style-appropriate sound, registration choice, text clarity, idiom awareness | Shared vocal standards remain, but observable style evidence shifts by idiom | Evidence differs by sound colour, registration, diction, attack/release | Specific register choice, sound colour, text clarity, idiom cue | Style label plus audible evidence | Medical/fach claims; overconfident style labelling | [MT-S072], [MT-S078] | Moderate | Partly |
| Acting-through-song | Lyric intention, phrase-level choice, body/facial expression, story clarity and speech-song continuity | Often deserves more explanatory weight than generic “voice quality” language | Evidence sits in lyric-by-lyric dramatic use, not only in overall emotion | Beat, lyric, phrase, target, focus, body use, dynamic/dramatic alignment | Exact lyric/phrase/beat and dramatic function | Generic “good storytelling” | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | High | No |

**Scoring Implications**

This section does **not** propose score-field changes or new weightings.

| Scoring area | Why it matters in MT | Suggested design implication | Source ID(s) | Confidence | Caution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting and vocal remain separate | MT evidence consistently treats acting and singing as co-central yet distinct | Keep both visible and evidence-led; do not collapse into one blended performance score | [MT-S004], [MT-S007], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | High | Preserve current six-field framework and MT weights |
| Dance / movement inside MT | Movement matters, but current baseline does not support a new MT dance score field | Require stronger movement evidence inside existing acting/technical/report structure when dance is present | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | High | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting** |
| Integration | MT is not just acting + singing reported separately | Require a visible integration judgement in commentary and timestamping, but not a new score field under the current baseline | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | High | Preserve baseline — revise only if compatible |
| Acting-through-song | Core MT-specific evidence sits inside both acting and vocal judgment | Make it a required evidence test inside existing acting/vocal comments, not a new field | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | High | No new score field |
| Vocal technique vs communication | Strong exam-board evidence separates these conceptually | Inside the current vocal area, require the assessor to distinguish technique from communication/story/style | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | High | Do not split the score field unless explicitly approved |
| Subtype/style | Style and route affect what evidence matters most | Capture subtype/style conditionally as report/evidence emphasis, not as a fixed subtype weighting or standalone score | [MT-S072], [MT-S078], [MT-S074], [MT-S070] | Moderate | **Feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting** |
| Self-tape assessability / fairness | Technical burden and access can distort evaluation if treated as talent | Keep assessability in technical/reliability language rather than as a hidden talent proxy | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | High | Do not penalise low-budget or access-adapted tapes unless assessability is materially blocked |
| Direction-response | Useful in recalls/workshops, but often not visible in a submitted tape | Suppress unless clearly observable or explicitly part of the task | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S070] | Moderate | Do not invent redirectability from a single finished take |
| Professional-readiness / training potential | Institutions and practitioners mention these, but they are easily overgeneralised | Keep most of this in report language and bounded role-fit notes, not as a broad score driver | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S054], [MT-S064] | Moderate | Avoid “commercial suitability” or marketability scoring |
| Exact exam-board percentages | Useful design comparators, not direct audition weights | Use only as comparator logic | [MT-S007], [MT-S009] | High | Do **not** import directly into MT scoring |

**Report-Structure Implications**

| Report section or feedback area | What it should require | Observable evidence required | Source basis | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Headline / casting insight | A material- and performer-specific differentiator | Specific lyric/beat, scene-to-song transition, style cue, or movement choice | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S072], [MT-S070] | High |
| Component breakdown | Explicit coverage of spoken acting, song, and any meaningful integration point | Acting moment, song moment, and at least one connection between them where present | [MT-S013], [MT-S045], [MT-S049], [MT-S011] | High |
| Acting note | Not just “grounded” or “connected”; must reference objective/listening/subtext or acting-through-song | Line/beat, relationship target, thought change, or sung-lyric action | [MT-S006], [MT-S045], [MT-S077] | High |
| Vocal note | Must distinguish technique, style, and communication/story | Phrase, register, diction, style/era cue, and storytelling function | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | High |
| Movement / dance note | Only where visible and assessable; must be full-body and style-aware where possible | Visible combo/pass, posture, rhythm, floor use, risk-taking, narrative movement | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | High |
| Strengths / improvements | Each item must be tied to a concrete performer choice or issue | Timestamp/moment, component, and why it mattered | [MT-S037], [MT-S045], [MT-S055] | High |
| Fix first / next take plan | Must be evidence-led and component-specific | One high-impact observed change, tied to actual material and subtype where relevant | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S077], [MT-S078] | High |
| Role fit / brief note | Must stay bounded to material, style and brief context, not identity-based fit | Brief-supported style/material demand, not “commercial suitability” | [MT-S046], [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | High |
| Self-tape assessability / reliability note | Must distinguish technical clarity from performance quality | Audibility, framing, movement visibility, accompaniment balance, access context if relevant | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | High |
| Fairness / access note | Must record non-penalisation where relevant | Access adjustments, limited setup, deadline or burden context if known | [MT-S055] | High |

## Guardrails and Compatibility

**Areas Not to Change Yet Because Evidence Is Insufficient**

| Area | Why evidence is insufficient | Source basis / evidence gap | Risk of changing now | How to handle in audit | Later research needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Through-composed MT rule set | No dedicated through-composed/public assessment source in the completed corpus | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Invented subtype rules | Keep visible as explicit evidence gap | Yes |
| Fixed weighting for dance-led / voice-led / acting-led MT | Evidence supports emphasis shifts, not fixed numeric weighting | [MT-S005], [MT-S007], [MT-S009], [MT-S070], [MT-S072] | Pseudo-precision and baseline instability | Use “feedback emphasis only — not enough evidence for fixed weighting” | Yes |
| Formal descriptors for jukebox / pop-rock / some contemporary MT | Evidence is subtype-useful but not descriptor-rich enough for formal scoring bands | [MT-S072], [MT-S078] | Overclaiming subtype precision | Use in report language only where observable | Yes |
| Deeper vocal-style calibration | Some style evidence is strong, but voice-health / deeper fach calibration is outside MT scope | [MT-S072], [MT-S007] | Overbuilding voice-specific rules inside MT | Defer to Voice/Singing research | Yes |
| Deeper dance-led calibration | MT-B4 adds useful dance evidence, but not a full dance-rubric substitute | [MT-S070], [MT-S051], [MT-S074] | Weak dance specificity dressed up as certainty | Defer to Dance research | Yes |
| Exact exam-board percentages | They are educational-framework-specific, not universal audition logic | [MT-S007], [MT-S009] | Inappropriate import into admissions/casting scoring | Treat as comparator only | No further MT research; design caution only |
| New score fields / schema changes | Outside audit scope and baseline-protected | 0E do-not-touch list | Baseline breakage | Do not change in MT revision unless separately authorised | No, unless system-level work is explicitly approved |

**Exclusions and Anti-Bias Guardrails**

| Excluded or cautious area | Where it might appear in rubric or feedback | Why it must not become a scoring criterion | Safer handling | Source basis from MT-SYN / baseline | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Body / type / appearance | Role fit, headline, professional_presentation | Creates discriminatory and marketability-led judging | Exclude entirely from scoring; if role fit exists, bound it to material/style/context only | [MT-S056], [MT-S064], 0E guardrails | High |
| Protected characteristics | First-round forms, role fit, presentation | Not legitimate performance criteria | Exclude entirely | [MT-S056], 0E guardrails | High |
| Nationality / passport / identity data | Slate/process notes | Administrative or discriminatory, not artistic quality | Exclude from scoring; do not import from older process guidance | [MT-S056] | High |
| Class-coded presentation | “Well-presented”, dress, home environment | Risks class bias and polish bias | Reframe only as assessability/readability if truly material | [MT-S058], 0E guardrails | High |
| Vague charisma / charm / “presence” | Acting / headline / verdict | Too subjective unless tied to specific observable behaviour | Reframe as focus, stillness, energy placement, clarity of action | [MT-S058], [MT-S064], [MT-S070] | High |
| Social-media behaviour | Professional-readiness or practitioner advice spillover | Not a tape-performance criterion | Exclude | [MT-S063] | High |
| Expensive tape production | Technical / presentation | Production value is not talent | Score only basic assessability; do not reward polish beyond readability | [MT-S055], [MT-S059], 0E guardrails | High |
| Access needs | Technical / presentation / reliability | Access adjustment is not weakness | Use fairness/access note; do not penalise | [MT-S055], 0E guardrails | High |
| Lack of studio polish | Technical / presentation | Can reflect resources, not ability | Only note when it materially blocks assessment | [MT-S055], [MT-S011], 0E guardrails | High |
| Tape-only vocal-health diagnosis | Vocal feedback | MT-SYN supports style and production observations, not diagnosis | Limit to observable sound/use; defer medical claims entirely | [MT-S072], 0E scoring guardrails | High |
| Marketability as talent proxy | Role fit / verdict | Confuses commercial taste with skill | Replace with observable preparation, fit to material/style, or suppress | [MT-S046], [MT-S055], [MT-S056] | High |
| “Perfect casting” logic | Role fit / professional-readiness | Penn State explicitly warns against it as the main artistic criterion | Distinguish professional potential from perfect casting | [MT-S046] | High |

| Recommendation ID | Baseline constraint affected | Compatible | Reason | Required handling | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MT-A01 | MT weights, acting/vocal visibility, component breakdown, consistency_modifier | Yes | Directly preserves the MT regression anchor | Preserve unchanged | High |
| MT-A02 | Six-field schema / no new score fields | Yes | Can be implemented as stronger evidence requirements inside existing acting/vocal logic | Do inside existing fields only | High |
| MT-A03 | Step 1 evidence / Step 2 text-only polish | Yes | Requires stronger evidence anchors, not pipeline changes | Preserve fixed pipeline | High |
| MT-A04 | Six-field schema / vocal field preserved | Yes | Distinguishes technique vs story within the current vocal area | No new vocal sub-score | High |
| MT-A05 | No new score fields / MT stabilisation | Yes | Movement specificity can be improved through evidence and report wording | Do not add MT dance score field | High |
| MT-A06 | Component breakdown / consistency_modifier | Yes | Integration can be made explicit in evidence and report structure | Preserve current breakdown and modifier | High |
| MT-A07 | No schema changes / subtype not guaranteed | Yes, with caution | Compatible if handled as conditional report/evidence logic only | Do not create subtype score fields or fixed weights | High |
| MT-A08 | Fairness, access, technical guardrails | Yes | Directly aligned with baseline fairness rules | Keep in reliability/report language | High |
| MT-A09 | Unsupported-claim handling | Yes | Prevents invented scoring criteria | Suppress unless observable | High |
| MT-A10 | Anti-bias guardrails / practitioner filtering | Yes | Aligns with baseline instruction not to score unsupported criteria | Keep most authenticity/professional-readiness language out of scoring unless evidenced | High |
| MT-A11 | Role-fit modifier bounds / brief mode only | Yes | Aligns with bounded role-fit and anti-bias constraints | Keep role fit brief-bounded and evidence-based | High |
| MT-A12 | Evidence-gap visibility / no invented criteria | Yes | Preserves uncertainty rather than inventing rules | Mark through-composed as unresolved | High |
| MT-A13 | Weight / threshold / schema do-not-touch | Yes | Explicitly prevents inappropriate import of exam-board percentages | Treat as comparator only | High |
| MT-A14 | Timestamp spread across components | Yes | Directly supports a preserved baseline requirement | Improve distribution, not schema | High |
| MT-A15 | Safety/fairness guardrails | Yes | Reinforces exclusions already required by baseline | Exclude bias-sensitive material from scoring | High |

**Evidence-to-Rubric Traceability Matrix**

| MT-SYN evidence finding | Source ID(s) | Rubric area affected | Audit implication | Recommendation ID(s) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acting-through-song must be evidenced, not implied | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Acting, vocal, timestamps, strengths/improvements | Require lyric/phrase/beat evidence for MT song judgment | MT-A02, MT-A03, MT-A14 | High |
| Voice should be judged in service of story and style | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | Vocal note, strengths, improvements | Separate technique from communication/story/style within current vocal area | MT-A04 | High |
| Dance notes need visible, story-linked movement evidence | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | Acting/technical commentary, timestamps | Suppress generic movement praise; require visible movement evidence | MT-A05, MT-A14 | High |
| Integration is core to MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | Component breakdown, overall insight, consistency logic | Require explicit integration commentary and scene/song continuity | MT-A06, MT-A14 | High |
| Self-tape fairness and access must shape reliability language | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | Technical, audio, professional_presentation, reliability language | Separate assessability/fairness from performance quality | MT-A08, MT-A15 | High |
| Training potential must not collapse into perfect casting logic | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S054] | Role fit, professional_presentation, verdict language | Bound training-potential language and suppress marketability logic | MT-A11 | High |
| Style / subtype handling is needed where observable | [MT-S072], [MT-S078], [MT-S074], [MT-S070] | Vocal, acting, component notes, timestamps | Capture subtype/style conditionally and with evidence | MT-A07 | Moderate |
| Practitioner material must be filtered for observability and bias | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S064], [MT-S065] | Acting, professional_presentation, role fit | Keep practitioner advice out of scoring unless observable and safe | MT-A10, MT-A15 | High |
| Through-composed MT remains partly unresolved | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Subtype logic, report language | Keep visible as evidence gap; do not invent subtype rules | MT-A12 | High |
| Exact exam-board percentages are comparators only | [MT-S007], [MT-S009] | Scoring logic | Do not import directly into MT scores | MT-A13 | High |

## Revision Handoff

**Recommendations Table**

| Recommendation ID | Rubric area | Current risk | Specific recommended change | Observable tape evidence assessor must cite | MT subtype affected | Source basis from MT-SYN | Evidence strength | Baseline impact | Priority | Implementation caution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MT-A01 | MT core structure | Regression of the stabilised MT anchor | Preserve current MT weights, visible acting/vocal categories, component breakdown, and consistency_modifier | Acting evidence and song evidence must both remain visible where present | All MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S007], [MT-S045], [MT-S049]; 0E guardrails | Strong | Preserve | High | Do not alter weights, schema, or component visibility |
| MT-A02 | Acting-through-song | Still implicit rather than required | Require MT song judgments to show acting-through-song evidence inside existing acting/vocal sections | Lyric beat, phrase action, target/relationship, focus/body change | All MT, especially acting-led | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Strong | Improve | High | No new score field |
| MT-A03 | Song storytelling specificity | Generic “good storytelling” risk | Require lyric / phrase / beat evidence whenever song storytelling is praised or criticised | Exact lyric or phrase and its dramatic function | All MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S077] | Strong | Improve | High | Keep evidence brief and observable |
| MT-A04 | Vocal area | Technique-only or generic vocal praise | Require the vocal area to distinguish technical accomplishment from communication/story/style, or state when only one is observable | Register, diction, phrase, style cue, textual clarity, story effect | Voice-led, Golden Age, contemporary, legit/mix/belt | [MT-S007], [MT-S072], [MT-S034] | Strong | Improve | High | Do not split the score field without approval |
| MT-A05 | Movement / dance comments | Generic movement praise and weak visibility checks | Require visible movement evidence before making dance-specific or movement-specific claims; suppress movement praise if the tape does not show enough | Full-body movement, posture, risk-taking, rhythm, choreography uptake, character through movement | Dance-led and integrated MT | [MT-S019], [MT-S070], [MT-S051] | Strong | Improve | High | No new dance score field; defer deeper calibration to Dance research |
| MT-A06 | Integration | Acting and song can still read as separate silos | Require one explicit integration comment when acting + song and/or movement are both present | Scene-to-song continuity, acting continuity in song, movement supporting lyric/story | All MT | [MT-S004], [MT-S009], [MT-S045], [MT-S049] | Strong | Improve | High | Use report language / evidence requirement, not a new score |
| MT-A07 | Style / subtype handling | No forced style specificity | Require subtype/style to be captured only where observable or task-known, and to shape evidence expectations rather than weights | Era/style cue, register choice, diction, movement vocabulary, non-imitation | Golden Age, contemporary, jukebox, dance-led / voice-led / acting-led, legit/mix/belt | [MT-S072], [MT-S078], [MT-S074], [MT-S070] | Moderate | Improve | High | No guessing, no subtype score field, no fixed weighting |
| MT-A08 | Self-tape assessability and fairness | Technical burden may be conflated with talent | Separate assessability/reliability from performance quality and explicitly non-penalise low-budget or access-adapted setups unless evidence is materially blocked | Audibility, framing, movement visibility, clarity of accompaniment, access context if relevant | All MT | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S011] | Strong | Improve | High | Keep this in reliability/technical language, not a talent proxy |
| MT-A09 | Direction-response | Could be scored when not visible | Suppress direction-response unless actual redirection, note application, or adjustment is observable | Alternate take, visible adjustment, recall note response, live redirect evidence | Recalls/workshops mainly | [MT-S056], [MT-S058], [MT-S065], [MT-S070] | Moderate | Suppress conditionally | High | Do not infer from a single fixed take |
| MT-A10 | Individuality / authenticity / professional-readiness | Can drift into charm or taste | Bound these concepts to observable choices and preparation; keep most of them in report language rather than standalone scoring | Distinct choice-making, ownership of lyric/text, prepared cuts, file discipline | All MT | [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S064], [MT-S065] | Moderate | Improve | High | Exclude vague charm/presence and marketability |
| MT-A11 | Role fit / casting language | “Commercial suitability” and “perfect casting” drift | Keep training potential distinct from casting suitability; allow role fit only as brief-bounded material/style/context fit | Material/style fit to the brief, strengths-led handling, not look/type | All MT | [MT-S046], [MT-S018], [MT-S054] | Strong | Suppress conditionally | High | Do not reward marketability, appearance, or identity-based fit |
| MT-A12 | Through-composed MT | Evidence gap may be papered over | Keep through-composed MT explicitly flagged as an unresolved evidence gap in the later revision step | If commented on at all, continuity/stamina/transition evidence only | Through-composed / sung-through | [MT-S066], [MT-S074], [MT-S079] | Evidence gap | Defer | High | Do not create subtype rules or weights yet |
| MT-A13 | Weighting logic | Exact exam-board percentages could be imported too literally | Treat exam-board percentages and domains as design comparators only, not direct scoring rules | N/A — comparator logic only | All MT | [MT-S007], [MT-S009] | Strong | Defer | High | No weight changes without explicit approval |
| MT-A14 | Timestamping and fix-first | MT notes can still under-cover one component or omit integration | Require MT timestamps and fix-first notes to cover acting, song, and at least one integration or style-specific moment where present | Timestamped acting moment, song moment, and integration/style moment | All MT | [MT-S013], [MT-S045], [MT-S049], [MT-S011] | Strong | Improve | High | Stay within baseline max of 8 timestamps |
| MT-A15 | Exclusion / anti-bias handling | Practitioner or role-fit language may leak unsafe criteria | Explicitly exclude body/type/appearance, protected identity data, social media, polish proxies, access needs, and tape-only vocal-health diagnosis from MT scoring | N/A — exclusion rule | All MT | [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S064], [MT-S072]; 0E guardrails | Strong | Remove | High | Keep exclusions visible in the revision step |

**Final Handoff for MT Revision**

The Run 0B Musical Theatre slice is broadly sound as a **baseline-preserving** object, and the audit does not support structural upheaval. The current strengths that must not regress are the protected MT anchor itself: the existing six-field framework, visible acting and vocal categories, current MT weights, multi-component detection, component breakdown, and timestamp spread across acting and song where possible. Those are aligned with the strongest official and exam-board evidence and are also explicitly protected by the Run 0E guardrail pack. Core preserve items therefore sit around [MT-S004], [MT-S007], [MT-S045], [MT-S049], [MT-S013] and the 0E MT stabilisation rules.

The highest-priority improvements are about **specificity inside the existing structure**, not about new score fields or new weighting models. The most urgent audit focus is acting-through-song: MT feedback should not be allowed to praise or criticise song performance without citing lyric-, phrase-, or beat-level evidence. This is strongly supported by [MT-S004], [MT-S006], and [MT-S077]. Closely linked to this, the vocal area needs a clearer internal distinction between **technical accomplishment** and **communication/story/style**, using evidence from [MT-S007], [MT-S072], and [MT-S034]. Movement notes also need to become more defensible: if the tape does not show visible, assessable movement, the rubric should not invite generic dance praise. Strongest support there comes from [MT-S019], [MT-S070], and [MT-S051].

The second major audit priority is **integration**. Musical Theatre should not read like separate acting feedback and singing feedback placed side by side. The later MT revision should check whether the component breakdown, timestamps, and fix-first logic force at least one integration comment when acting and song coexist, grounded in scene-to-song continuity, acting continuity inside song, or movement in service of lyric/story. Key evidence sits in [MT-S004], [MT-S009], [MT-S045], and [MT-S049].

The third priority is **fairness, non-penalisation, and filtering**. Self-tape assessability must be separated from performance quality, and low-budget or access-adapted tapes must not be treated as weaker talent evidence unless assessability is materially blocked. That boundary is strongest in [MT-S055], [MT-S056], and [MT-S011]. Practitioner material should also be filtered: authenticity, individuality, preparation and direction-response are useful only where tied to observable evidence; body/type/appearance, passport/nationality, social media, charm, marketability, generic “presence,” and tape-only vocal-health diagnosis must stay out. This exclusion work is grounded in [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S064], [MT-S072], and the 0E anti-bias guardrails.

Subtype/style handling should be improved, but only conditionally. The evidence supports style-aware report language for Golden Age versus contemporary, legit/mix/belt, jukebox, and acting-led / voice-led / dance-led emphasis through [MT-S072], [MT-S078], [MT-S074], [MT-S070], and [MT-S077]. It does **not** support fixed subtype weightings, new subtype score fields, or a solved framework for through-composed MT. Through-composed remains an explicit evidence gap anchored by [MT-S066], [MT-S074], and [MT-S079], and the later revision must keep that limitation visible rather than filling it by inference.

In short, the later MT revision should: preserve the stabilised MT core, strengthen evidence requirements, make acting-through-song and integration structurally unavoidable in commentary, separate fairness from quality, capture subtype/style only where observable, suppress direction-response unless visible, exclude bias-sensitive material, and defer fixed weighting or deeper dance/voice design changes to later discipline-specific research.{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\cocoartf2868

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Core Musical Theatre discipline logic\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Musical Theatre assessment depends on multi-component performance evidence, usually an 
\f0\b acting scene plus song
\f1\b0 . The existing component detection, component breakdown and 
\f2\fs26 consistency_modifier
\f1\fs24  remain central and must not be weakened.\
Where the tape contains both acting and song, the report should distinguish:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls1\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	1	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
spoken scene work\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	2	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
sung performance\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	3	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
acting-through-song\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	4	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
transition or continuity between scene and song\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	5	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
any visible movement/dance evidence where present and assessable\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	6	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
any style/subtype evidence that is task-known or clearly observable\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Musical Theatre must not be treated as generic acting plus generic singing. The assessment should look for how acting, singing and movement combine to carry story, character, relationship, lyric intention and style.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Acting evidence requirements\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Acting feedback should cover observable performance choices such as:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls2\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
objective or action\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
relationship target\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
listening or response\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
thought shift\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
beat change\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
subtext\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
stakes\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
stillness or focus\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
eyeline or camera/reader relationship\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
scene-to-song continuity\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
acting choices inside sung material\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Spoken acting notes should be tied to a specific line, beat, reaction, transition or moment of decision. Avoid generic comments such as \'93strong acting\'94, \'93more confidence\'94 or \'93good presence\'94 unless the report names the behaviour that created that effect.\
Where no brief exists, the report must not invent role expectations or production-world requirements.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Acting-through-song evidence requirements\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Acting-through-song is now a required Musical Theatre evidence test inside the existing acting, vocal and component commentary.\
When praising or criticising a song performance, the report must cite at least one observable song-specific acting detail where available, such as:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls3\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
lyric beat\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
phrase change\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
objective or action carried through the lyric\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
imagined relationship or addressee\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
focus shift\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
breath or dynamic choice with dramatic function\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
body/facial expression supporting the lyric\
\ls3\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
continuity or drop between spoken scene and sung material\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Generic \'93good storytelling\'94 is insufficient unless anchored to lyric-, phrase- or beat-level evidence.\
Acceptable wording pattern:\
\'93In the song, the storytelling became clearer at the phrase where the performer redirected the lyric towards the imagined partner, using a quieter attack and steadier eyeline to show the objective changing.\'94\
Unacceptable wording pattern:\
\'93The song had good storytelling.\'94\
If lyric / phrase / beat evidence is not available or the song component is too technically unclear to assess, the report should avoid broad claims about song storytelling and instead state the evidence limitation.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Vocal evidence requirements\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The vocal category remains a single score field, but MT vocal feedback must distinguish, where observable, between:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls4\ilvl0
\f0\b \cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	1	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
technical accomplishment
\f1\b0 \uc0\u8232 Examples: breath use, diction, register choice, line, resonance, placement, tone, support, range handling, rhythmic accuracy, pitch security.\
\ls4\ilvl0
\f0\b \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	2	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
communication / story / style function
\f1\b0 \uc0\u8232 Examples: lyric clarity, phrase intention, style/era awareness, character-driven sound, dynamic shape, textual emphasis, whether vocal choices served the dramatic moment.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 The report should not use \'93strong voice\'94 as a standalone conclusion. It should name the technical and/or communicative evidence that made the singing effective or limited.\
Acceptable evidence includes:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls5\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
register event\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
diction choice\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
phrase shape\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
breath or sustain moment\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
style or era cue\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
text clarity\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
vocal colour serving character or lyric\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
contrast between technical security and storytelling impact\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Do not diagnose vocal health from tape. Do not make medical, fach or long-term sustainability claims. Limit vocal comments to observable sound, use and performance function.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Song storytelling and lyric specificity\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Whenever song storytelling is praised or criticised, the report must cite the actual moment that supports the claim. Evidence may include:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls6\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a lyric phrase\
\ls6\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a musical phrase\
\ls6\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a breath or pause before a line\
\ls6\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a shift in dynamic, tempo, focus or physicality\
\ls6\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a change in relationship target\
\ls6\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a contrast between verse/chorus, section A/B, or spoken/sung material\
\ls6\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a moment where vocal technique either supported or obscured the lyric\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 The report should make clear whether the issue is primarily:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls7\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
vocal technique\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
lyric understanding\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
acting-through-song\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
style fit\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
transition/continuity\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
audio/technical assessability\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 This prevents song feedback from collapsing into vague praise or a purely vocal-technical judgement.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Movement and dance evidence requirements\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Movement and dance comments are permitted only where the tape shows enough visible, assessable movement evidence.\
Movement feedback should cite observable details such as:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls8\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
full-body visibility\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
rhythm or musicality\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
posture or alignment as readable on tape\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
transition quality\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
physical attack or release\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
risk-taking where visible\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
choreography uptake where visible\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
character or story carried through movement\
\ls8\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
movement vocabulary where the style is clear or briefed\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Do not use generic phrases such as \'93nice movement\'94 or \'93good energy\'94 without naming the visible movement moment and its function.\
If the tape does not show enough of the body, space or choreography to judge movement fairly, the report should suppress dance-specific claims and may instead note the assessability limitation. This must not penalise disability, mobility aids, seated adaptation, access needs or reduced range of motion. Only assess what is visible and relevant to the submitted task.\
No MT dance score field is added. Deeper movement calibration remains deferred to the Dance branch.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Integration and component breakdown requirements\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The component breakdown must not read as separate acting and singing reports pasted together.\
Where acting and song are both present, the report should include at least one explicit integration comment, grounded in observable evidence such as:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls9\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
scene-to-song transition\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
continuity of character from spoken text into song\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
acting intention maintained through vocal demands\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
lyric/story supported by movement\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
contrast between spoken acting and sung acting\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
consistency or inconsistency across components\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
whether the performer\'92s strongest component supported or disrupted the whole MT presentation\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 The 
\f2\fs26 consistency_modifier
\f1\fs24  remains protected. It should continue to help capture whether the acting, vocal and component-level evidence align or diverge across the tape.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Timestamp and fix-first requirements\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Timestamped notes should cover both acting and song where possible. Within the existing timestamp limit, MT timestamping should aim to include:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls10\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	1	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
one spoken acting moment, if present\
\ls10\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	2	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
one song/vocal moment, if present\
\ls10\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	3	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
one acting-through-song, integration, transition, movement or style-specific moment, if present and assessable\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 If one component is absent, too short, technically blocked or not assessable, the report should not invent coverage. It should state the limitation in reliability, technical, audio or component language as appropriate.\
Fix-first and next-take notes must be evidence-led and component-specific. They should identify the highest-impact observable adjustment, such as:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls11\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
clarifying the objective in a spoken beat\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
anchoring a lyric phrase to a clearer addressee\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
improving diction on a story-critical phrase\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
stabilising the scene-to-song transition\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
making movement more readable in frame\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
separating technical singing work from lyric/story work\
\ls11\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
improving accompaniment balance where audio blocks judgement\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Generic fix-first advice such as \'93bring more energy\'94, \'93connect more\'94 or \'93be more confident\'94 should be avoided unless translated into a specific action tied to the submitted material.\
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3 \cf0 \uc0\u11835 
\f1 \
\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 Style and subtype handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 MT subtype or style may shape feedback emphasis only when it is:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls12\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
stated in the brief\
\ls12\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
obvious from the material\
\ls12\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
visible/audible in the tape\
\ls12\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
necessary to explain the performance evidence\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Supported conditional style language may include:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls13\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
Golden Age\
\ls13\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
contemporary MT\
\ls13\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
legit\
\ls13\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
mix\
\ls13\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
belt\
\ls13\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
pop-rock\
\ls13\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
jukebox\

\f0\b\fs48 \cf0 7. Final Addendum to Attach to MT-REV\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Attach the following block to the revised MT slice before product/prompt implementation.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 MT final audit output-specificity addendum\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Musical Theatre report must satisfy the following output-specificity checks in addition to the revised rubric wording.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Headline / casting insight\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The headline or casting insight must include at least one tape-specific differentiator, such as:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls1\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
the material, role or component\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a specific acting, song, movement or transition choice\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
the performer\'92s strongest observable differentiator\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
a style/subtype cue where known or clearly observable\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Avoid broad headline language such as \'93technically strong and emotionally connected\'94 unless it is immediately tied to this performer, this tape, this material and an observable moment.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Timestamp density\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 For an assessable 
\f0\b 3\'965 minute Musical Theatre or hybrid tape
\f1\b0 , the system should aim for 
\f0\b 5\'968 timestamped notes
\f1\b0 , while preserving the Run 0E maximum of 
\f0\b 8
\f1\b0 .\
Where acting and song are both present and assessable, timestamped notes should normally include:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls2\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	1	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
at least one spoken acting moment\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	2	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
at least one song/vocal moment\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	3	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
at least one acting-through-song, integration, transition, movement or style-specific moment\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	4	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
at least one strength moment\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	5	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
at least one improvement or fix-first moment\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Shorter tapes, blocked evidence, poor audio, poor visibility or genuinely low-evidence submissions may justify fewer notes, but the report should not under-produce timestamps on a clearly assessable multi-component tape.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Next-take plan: rehearsal versus recorded take\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Where the next-take plan suggests physical action, props, movement, staging or framing, it must distinguish between:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls3\ilvl0
\f0\b \cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
rehearsal-only exercises
\f1\b0 , and\
\ls3\ilvl0
\f0\b \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
recorded-take changes
\f1\b0  that are safe and compatible with the brief.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Do not suggest walking, props, additional staging or frame-breaking movement where the brief requires fixed framing, head-and-shoulders framing, minimal movement or a simple self-tape setup.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Assessability and caps\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Separating assessability from performance quality does 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  override existing TapeCoach caps, blockers or reliability logic.\
If audio, visibility, framing, file handling or technical setup materially blocks assessment, the report may:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls4\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
lower technical/audio/professional-standard scores where appropriate\
\ls4\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
reduce feedback reliability\
\ls4\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
trigger existing caps or blockers where applicable\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 But it must not describe access-adapted, low-budget or home-recorded conditions as weaker talent evidence unless the submitted performance is materially unassessable.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Professional presentation weighting clarity\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f3\b0\fs26 \cf0 professional_presentation
\f1\fs24  remains part of the six operational score-field system and report logic. The MT final score formula remains unchanged:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\partightenfactor0
\ls5\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
acting 30%\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
vocal 30%\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
brief_adherence 15%\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
technical 15%\
\ls5\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
audio 10%\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Do not introduce a new weighted professional-presentation component for Musical Theatre unless explicitly approved elsewhere.\
\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 4. Branch Scope and Production Context\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Musical Theatre branch covers self-tape evaluation where acting and song are present, usually as a multi-component audition containing an acting scene and a song. It also covers MT-specific report behaviour around acting-through-song, vocal technique in service of story, scene-to-song integration, movement in service of story where visible, style/subtype language where observable, and fairness/access constraints.\
The completed revised MT outputs are intended to improve report specificity inside the existing TapeCoach architecture. They are not intended to change the scoring model, weights, score fields, audition types, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds, role-fit bounds, report schema, backend pipeline or UI mechanisms.\
Current live production behaviour remains separate. The four supplied current MT outputs preserve the core Acting + Song structure, but they do not yet satisfy the v5 output-specificity standard. The revision and output-specificity patch are requirements for future implementation planning; they are not evidence that production has already changed.\
The branch must preserve the live system\'92s six score fields, current MT weights, acting + song detection, component breakdown, visible Acting and Vocal categories, consistency_modifier, timestamp coverage across acting and song, UK terminology, maximum 3 strengths, maximum 3 improvements and maximum 8 timestamped notes.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0
