\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Adversarial / non-regression tests: MT-V5-OST01\'96OST27 cover acting + song, no-brief MT, song-only and acting-only leakage, fixed/choice material, generic praise suppression, timestamp imbalance, false specificity, production polish, poor audio, access-adapted MT, callback/workshop overclaim, comparison mismatch and export timestamp mismatch.\
Display-layer checks: MT-V5-LQA01\'96LQA24 cover raw JSON, rendered report, PDF/export, comparison page, category/component labels, Vocal/Acting visibility, timestamp parity, score/verdict consistency, brief-mode consistency, role-fit suppression, reliability, presentation notes, technical signals and access-adapted output handling.\
Generic-feedback suppression: MT-V5-OSP01\'96OSP35 cover generic acting/vocal/movement/musicality phrases, recall/callback/castability overclaims, false-perfect-adherence language, alternative-repertoire leakage, polish/resource merit, access-deficit language and live-room inference.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 10. Live Output QA / Bridge QA Status\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 True current MT report artefacts were supplied as four PDF/report captures or excerpts. Live-output QA was completed at 
\f0\b partial PDF/report level
\f1\b0 . It was not full production release QA because raw JSON, comparison-page artefacts, separate rendered/export parity artefacts and score-recompute traces were not supplied.\
The four artefacts preserve the core MT anchor: Acting Scene and Song are visible, Vocal appears where singing exists, Acting appears where spoken acting exists, and component breakdown is displayed. However, current outputs fail MT-V5 output-specificity QA due to generic praise, unanchored acting-through-song, broad vocal praise, timestamp underproduction, brief/no-brief contradiction, readiness inconsistency and live-room/casting overclaims. Examples include \'93recall-worthy\'94 and only two timestamps in A01, the brief/no-brief contradiction and \'93WHY THIS ISN\'92T READY\'94 in A02, \'93strong callback potential\'94 and page-side claims in A03, and \'93highly castable for contemporary musical theatre workshops\'94 in A04.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 14. Patch / Retest Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 Decision: No further branch research or rubric patch is required before cross-branch consolidation. The completed MT output-specificity patch and live-output QA failures must be carried into consolidation as P0 implementation-planning and retest requirements.
\f1\b0 \
Rationale:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\ls1\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 MT source research, synthesis, gap audit, revision, final audit and output-specificity mapping are complete.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 The branch should not be reopened for broad research or rubric rework.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Current live outputs fail the MT-V5 output-specificity standard, but that is an enforcement and QA problem, not a source-maturity problem.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Cross-branch consolidation can proceed if it carries forward the MT output-rule corrections and release blockers explicitly.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Production release sign-off must not proceed until corrected MT outputs pass live-output QA.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Patch scope, if treated operationally: output-rule enforcement, generic phrase suppression, timestamp density, brief/no-brief consistency, fixed-material boundaries, role-fit/callback suppression, presentation anti-polish handling, display/JSON/export parity QA.\
What must not be reopened: MT source research, MT weights, six score fields, subtype weights, backend/schema/data-flow, caps/blockers/verdict thresholds, role-fit bounds, component detection architecture.\
Deep Research required: no.\
Standard ChatGPT sufficient: yes, for handoff, consolidation, QA mapping and implementation-planning requirements.\
Live outputs required for retest: yes. Required artefacts include raw JSON, rendered report, PDF/export, comparison page, score/verdict/cap trace and access-adapted MT output.\
Required retests: MT-V5-OST01\'96OST27 and MT-V5-LQA01\'96LQA24, prioritising no-brief MT, brief-mode contradiction, timestamp density, generic praise suppression, callback/castability suppression and JSON/render/export parity.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 15. Compact Branch Handoff Pack\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Musical Theatre is complete at research, synthesis, audit, revision, final-audit and output-specificity mapping level. The strongest branch asset remains the stabilised MT anchor: musical_theatre detection where acting + song are present, acting and song component breakdown, visible Acting and Vocal categories, current MT weights, consistency_modifier where used, and timestamp coverage across acting and song. This must not regress.\
The evidence base is strong. Official admissions sources such as MT-B1-002, MT-B1-005, MT-B1-006, MT-B1-009, MT-B1-020, MT-B1-023, MT-B1-030 and [MT-S046] support audition task structure, acting + song evidence, training-potential language and the distinction between potential and perfect casting. Exam-board sources [MT-S004], [MT-S006], [MT-S007] and [MT-S009] support acting-through-song, vocal technique versus interpretation/communication, and performance/technique/reflection distinctions. Practitioner and fairness sources [MT-S055], [MT-S056], [MT-S057], [MT-S058], [MT-S064] and [MT-S065] support access, burden, authenticity and direction-response boundaries only where observable. Subtype/pedagogy sources [MT-S070], [MT-S072], [MT-S074], [MT-S077], [MT-S078] and [MT-S079] support style-aware report language but not fixed weights.\
MT-A01\'96MT-A15 were addressed in MT-REV and passed final audit. The revision preserved the six-field scoring model, current MT weights, Step 1 / Step 2 split, report schema, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds and role-fit bounds. It strengthened acting-through-song, lyric/phrase/beat evidence, vocal story/style distinctions, movement visibility, integration, self-tape assessability, anti-polish handling and anti-bias exclusions. Through-composed MT, fixed subtype weighting, deeper dance calibration and deeper vocal-style calibration remain deferred.\
The output-specificity package is complete through MT-V5-OSR01\'96OSR17, MT-V5-OSP patterns, MT-V5-OSA evidence anchors, MT-V5-OST tests and MT-V5-LQA requirements. However, current live MT outputs fail output-specificity QA. Four PDF/report artefacts preserve MT component structure but show generic praise, unanchored acting-through-song/vocal claims, timestamp underproduction, brief/no-brief contradiction, readiness inconsistency and callback/castability overclaims. Raw JSON, comparison-page parity, renderer/export timestamp parity and score recomputation traces are not verified.\
Decision: MT is ready for cross-branch consolidation as a completed research/revision branch with a mandatory output-enforcement and live-QA retest item. It is not ready for production release sign-off until corrected outputs pass MT-V5 live-output QA.\
Stable ID families used: MT-S###, MT-A##, MT-V5-I##, MT-V5-P##, MT-V5-OSR##, MT-V5-OSP##, MT-V5-OSA##, MT-V5-OST##, MT-V5-LQA##, MT-V5-LIVE-##.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f2\b0\fs26 \cf0 \strokec2 AUDIT-STAGE LESSONS-LEARNED ADDENDUM\
\
Before auditing, perform an audit-specific input and alias check even if the synthesis already did one.\
\
Required audit readiness checks:\
- discipline synthesis handoff present: yes/no\
- rubric slice under audit present: yes/no\
- baseline / guardrail pack present: yes/no\
- optional prior or later rubric versions present: yes/no\
- exact rubric version under audit\
- whether optional versions are context only\
- whether audit may proceed\
- any input ambiguity\
- any source ID alias issues\
- any evidence gaps that constrain the audit\
- whether any high-priority recommendation would depend on unclear or weak evidence\
\
SOURCE ALIAS AND COUNTING RULE\
\
If the synthesis used legacy IDs but repaired IDs are available in the pasted material, create an audit-stage Source ID Alias Map.\
\
Rules:\
1. Treat matching source names and raw URLs as one source group.\
2. Prefer repaired global IDs where available.\
3. Preserve legacy IDs in the notes column.\
4. Do not double-count legacy and repaired versions of the same source.\
5. State whether the source-group count is exact, normalised, or approximate.\
6. Do not make high-priority recommendations from a source whose provenance or identity is unclear.\
\
RECOMMENDATION TRACEABILITY RULE\
\
Every audit recommendation must have:\
- stable recommendation ID\
- rubric area\
- current risk\
- specific recommended change\
- observable evidence the assessor must cite\
- subtype/style affected, if relevant\
- source basis from the synthesis handoff\
- evidence strength\
- baseline impact: preserve / improve / replace / remove / suppress conditionally / defer\
- priority\
- implementation caution\
\
High-priority recommendations must be supported by:\
- at least one high-confidence source, or\
- multiple converging medium-confidence sources, and\
- no unresolved provenance issue.\
\
BASELINE COMPATIBILITY RULE\
\
After the recommendations table, produce a Baseline Compatibility Check.\
\
For each recommendation, state:\
- baseline constraint affected\
- compatible: yes/no\
- reason\
- required handling\
- priority\
\
If a recommendation would require backend, schema, pipeline, database, data-flow, scoring-field, or fixed-weight changes not explicitly authorised, mark it:\
\'93defer\'94 or \'93preserve baseline \'97 revise only if compatible.\'94\
\
EVIDENCE-TO-RUBRIC TRACEABILITY MATRIX\
\
Before the final handoff, include a matrix:\
\
- synthesis evidence finding\
- Source ID(s)\
- rubric area affected\
- audit implication\
- recommendation ID(s)\
- confidence\
\
This prevents recommendations from becoming detached from the evidence base.\
\
DO-NOT-CHANGE SECTION\
\
Include a section called:\
\'93Areas Not to Change Yet Because Evidence Is Insufficient\'94\
\
Use this for:\
- unresolved subtype/style areas\
- fixed weighting claims not supported by evidence\
- discipline-specific details deferred to later research\
- practitioner opinion that is too subjective\
- pedagogy/context sources that do not support formal scoring\
- any proposed change that would break baseline constraints\
\
FINAL AUDIT HANDOFF REQUIREMENT\
\
The final audit handoff must be revision-ready.\
\
It must clearly separate:\
- preserve\
- improve\
- suppress conditionally\
- remove\
- defer\
- evidence gaps\
- anti-bias exclusions\
- non-regression constraints\
- recommendation IDs to carry into revision\
\
Do not rewrite the rubric.\
Do not create final wording.\
Do not implement changes.\
\pard\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0

\f2\b0\fs26 \cf0 \strokec2 REVISION TRACEABILITY ADDENDUM\
\
Use the audit recommendation IDs as the control system.\
\
Before revising:\
1. List all audit recommendation IDs.\
2. Classify each as:\
   - implement\
   - preserve only\
   - suppress conditionally\
   - remove\
   - defer\
   - not implemented because baseline-incompatible\
3. Do not implement any recommendation marked defer.\
4. Do not implement any recommendation that requires unauthorised schema, backend, scoring-field, weighting, pipeline, database, or data-flow changes.\
5. Do not implement any recommendation based only on weak, unclear, or unresolved evidence.\
\
For every implemented change, provide:\
- recommendation ID\
- rubric area changed\
- what changed\
- source basis\
- baseline compatibility\
- why it does not regress stabilised behaviour\
\
For every recommendation not implemented, provide:\
- recommendation ID\
- reason not implemented\
- whether it remains a future research gap, baseline constraint, or final-audit watch item\
\
Revision must preserve:\
- stabilised rubric structure\
- protected weights unless explicitly authorised\
- existing working behaviours\
- component detection logic\
- timestamp constraints\
- safety and anti-bias guardrails\
- separation of assessability from performance quality\
\
Revision must not:\
- rewrite beyond the audited slice\
- invent unsupported subtype criteria\
- import exact external weighting systems\
- create new score fields unless explicitly authorised\
- turn practitioner taste into scoring\
- penalise access needs or resource limitations\
\pard\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0

\f0\fs24 \cf3 \strokec3 \
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f1\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 Add this to the final audit prompt after each discipline revision\
\pard\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0

\f2\b0\fs26 \cf0 \strokec2 FINAL AUDIT / NON-REGRESSION CHECK\
\
This is a final audit step, not a research, synthesis, or rewrite step.\
\
Use only:\
1. The discipline audit handoff\
2. The revised discipline rubric slice\
3. The original rubric slice under audit\
4. The baseline / guardrail pack\
5. Optional prior versions only for regression context\
\
Task:\
Verify that the revision implemented the approved audit recommendations without regression.\
\
Required output:\
\
1. Input check\
   - audit handoff present\
   - original rubric slice present\
   - revised rubric slice present\
   - baseline guardrail pack present\
   - optional versions present\
   - exact revised version being audited\
\
2. Recommendation implementation matrix\
   - recommendation ID\
   - audit recommendation summary\
   - implemented: yes / partial / no / over-implemented\
   - evidence in revised rubric\
   - baseline-compatible: yes/no\
   - issue if any\
\
3. Non-regression check\
   - preserved stabilised behaviours\
   - any broken baseline constraints\
   - any unauthorised score-field, weighting, schema, backend, pipeline, database, or data-flow changes\
   - any missing preserve items\
\
4. Overreach check\
   - unsupported criteria introduced\
   - fixed weighting changes introduced without evidence\
   - practitioner taste converted into scoring\
   - pedagogy/context treated as formal scoring\
   - access or technical limitations penalised incorrectly\
\
5. Generic-feedback check\
   Apply the benchmark:\
   \'93Could this feedback only have been written about this specific tape, performer, material, style/subtype, and observable evidence?\'94\
\
6. Remaining issues\
   - must fix before finalising\
   - acceptable limitations\
   - deferred evidence gaps\
\
7. Final decision\
   - pass\
   - pass with minor issues\
   - revision required\
   - blocked by regression\
\
Do not rewrite the rubric unless explicitly requested.\
Do not create new recommendations unless needed to identify a regression or unresolved implementation issue.\
\pard\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0

\f0\b \cf0 \strokec2 Maturity audit caveat:
\f1\b0  the MT branch is auditable at research / synthesis / audit / revision / final-audit level. It is only 
\f0\b partly auditable at live-output level
\f1\b0  because the supplied PDFs show rendered report behaviour, but not raw JSON, comparison-page behaviour, renderer/export parity, or score-recomputation traces. The PDFs are still useful because they expose live-output risks: generic MT praise, timestamp under-density, brief/no-brief inconsistency, role-fit overclaiming, and possible production-polish drift. For example, one report shows \'93brief-driven mode\'94 while later technical signals say \'93No brief\'94, and it simultaneously gives a \'93Strong for this level\'94 verdict plus \'93WHY THIS ISN\'92T READY\'94.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 3. Scope and Non-Reopening Boundary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This maturity audit covers whether the 
\f0\b completed MT branch
\f1\b0  meets the later v5 standard around traceability, output specificity, field semantics, anti-bias boundaries, source-family discipline, and live-output readiness.\
It does 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  cover new research, new source extraction, rewritten rubric text, backend implementation, schema changes, scoring-field changes, weighting changes, cap changes, blocker changes, verdict-threshold changes, role-fit bound changes, UI design, pipeline design, or code.\
A 
\f0\b targeted MT patch
\f1\b0  is justified if the issue is already evidenced by the MT branch or supplied outputs and can be fixed through output-specificity / report-behaviour rules without reopening research.\
A 
\f0\b targeted source refresh
\f1\b0  is justified only if the desired behaviour requires new evidence, such as a complete through-composed MT framework or deeper pop-rock / belt / mix / dance-led scoring descriptors.\
A 
\f0\b broader MT v5 refresh
\f1\b0  would be justified only if the traceability chain were broken, the branch used unclear sources for major recommendations, or the revised branch conflicted with later v5 baseline standards. That is 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  the case here.\
The following must remain preserved: acting + song detection, component breakdown, visible Acting and Vocal categories, current MT weights, six-field model, consistency_modifier, timestamp coverage across acting and song, Step 1 evidence / Step 2 polish split, fixed-material guardrails, and anti-bias / accessibility protections.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 4. Later-Branch Maturity Standard\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 14. MT Maturity Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 Decision:
\f1\b0  MT branch remains usable but needs an 
\f0\b output-specificity patch
\f1\b0  before being treated as fully closed under the later v5 standard.\

\f0\b Rationale:
\f1\b0  the research, synthesis, audit, revision and final audit chain is strong enough. The branch does 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  need broader reopening, and no immediate targeted source refresh is required. The main weakness is that MT was completed before later branches established the mature standalone output-specificity and live-output QA pattern. The supplied PDFs confirm this risk: current rendered reports still contain generic MT praise, timestamp under-density, false-specificity risks, alternative repertoire advice, and role-fit / callback overclaims.\

\f0\b Critical blockers:
\f1\b0 \uc0\u8232 MT-V5-I07 and MT-V5-I09 are the most serious live-output risks: contradictory brief/no-brief handling and readiness/verdict inconsistency. MT-V5-I01, MT-V5-I03 and MT-V5-I11 are high-priority output-quality blockers: generic acting-through-song / vocal feedback and under-produced timestamps.\

\f0\b Can remain closed:
\f1\b0  MT source research, synthesis, gap audit, revision, and final audit do not need reopening.\

\f0\b Must be patched:
\f1\b0  output-specificity rules, generic suppression, timestamp density, fixed-material boundary, no-brief false-specificity, role-fit/callback claim scope, presentation/polish handling, and live-output QA requirements.\

\f0\b Must be researched only if expanding scope:
\f1\b0  complete through-composed MT rules or deeper pop-rock / belt / mix / dance-led formal descriptors.\

\f0\b Can MT proceed into cross-branch implementation planning before the patch?
\f1\b0  No, not as a fully mature closed branch. It can proceed only if the listed MT output-specificity patch is included as a prerequisite package.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 15. Reusable Handoff Pack for MT Patch or Confirmation\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 MT-V5 maturity handoff summary
\f1\b0 \
The Musical Theatre branch is mature at research, synthesis, audit, revision and final-audit level, but not yet mature at the later v5 output-specificity standard. The original MT branch correctly preserved the stabilised MT anchor: acting + song detection, component breakdown, visible Acting and Vocal categories, MT weights, consistency_modifier, and timestamp coverage requirements. The research basis is also strong: acting-through-song, vocal technique in service of story, integration, self-tape fairness and style/subtype limitations are all traceable through source IDs and MT-A01\'96MT-A15.\
The issue is not source maturity or rubric-slice maturity. The issue is output behaviour. The supplied PDFs show that current MT reports can still produce broad phrases such as \'93emotionally connected\'94, \'93strong vocal performance\'94, \'93grounded acting\'94, \'93good storytelling\'94, and \'93polished\'94 without enough lyric-, phrase-, beat-, style- or component-specific evidence. Several outputs provide only two to four timestamped notes for multi-component MT reports, below the v5 target for clearly assessable 3\'965 minute tapes. One report has a serious brief/no-brief contradiction and readiness inconsistency: it is brief-driven, says \'93WHY THIS ISN\'92T READY\'94, but also shows a strong verdict and later says no brief was provided. Another output gives alternative repertoire advice despite the fixed/submitted-material improvement context. These are output-specificity and QA problems, not reasons to reopen MT research.\
The recommended decision is: 
\f0\b MT remains usable but needs an output-specificity patch before cross-branch implementation planning.
\f1\b0  The patch should convert the final audit addendum into a standalone MT output-specificity handoff with adversarial tests. It should force lyric/phrase/beat evidence, distinguish vocal technique from story/style, require component-balanced timestamps, block unsupported no-brief specificity, suppress alternative-material advice in fixed-material contexts, bound role-fit / callback / workshop claims, and treat presentation as assessability rather than polish. It should also define live-output QA requirements for PDFs, JSON, comparison pages and renderer/export timestamp parity.\

\f0\b \cf0 \strokec2 Source / evidence gap summary
\f1\b0 \
No immediate new source research is required. Through-composed MT remains an explicit limitation. Targeted source refresh is only needed if the product wants a complete through-composed or deeper pop-rock / style-specific MT framework.\

\f0\b Output-specificity gap summary
\f1\b0 \
The gap is live-output enforcement: current reports still show generic praise, under-anchored song feedback, insufficient timestamp density, false-brief risk, and overconfident role-fit/callback language.\

\f0\b Non-regression test summary
\f1\b0 \
Regression tests must cover acting + song brief mode, no-brief MT mode, song-only, acting-only, fixed material, choice material, acting-through-song missing evidence, vocal-technique over-focus, transition ignored, timestamp imbalance, generic praise, alternative repertoire, production-polish bias, simple home capture, poor audio, movement/framing risk, access-adapted MT, comparison label mismatch, and rendered/export timestamp mismatch.\

\f0\b Final maturity decision
\f1\b0 \
MT is 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  a broader refresh case. It is a 
\f0\b targeted output-specificity patch
\f1\b0  case.\

\f0\b Auditable from supplied materials
\f1\b0 \
Research traceability, source-family boundaries, audit/revision/final-audit chain, baseline preservation, and partial live-output risks.\

\f0\b Not fully auditable from supplied materials
\f1\b0 \
Raw JSON behaviour, comparison-page parity, renderer/export parity, full label-helper behaviour, score recomputation traces, and access-adapted MT live-output behaviour.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 3. QA Scope and Non-Implementation Boundary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This QA covers visible PDF/rendered report behaviour: wording specificity, component display, Acting/Vocal visibility, timestamp density, brief/no-brief consistency, readiness/verdict consistency, role-fit/callback overclaims, generic praise, fixed-material leakage, presentation/polish boundaries, and visible technical-signal contradictions.\
It does 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  cover raw report JSON, score recomputation, caps/blockers as implemented, role-fit modifier calculation, comparison page parity, renderer/export parity, frontend label helper behaviour, pipeline behaviour, or persistence.\
A 
\f0\b pass
\f1\b0  means the visible report follows MT-V5 output rules with no material contradiction and enough evidence anchoring. A 
\f0\b partial pass
\f1\b0  means the MT stabilised structure is present but wording or density needs verification. A 
\f0\b fail
\f1\b0  means output-specificity or non-regression rules are visibly violated. 
\f0\b Not auditable
\f1\b0  means the required artefact is absent.\
Release sign-off is blocked by critical contradictions, unsafe overclaims, unsupported brief specificity, repeated generic-output failures, and missing parity artefacts. Implementation-planning follow-up may proceed only as requirements and verification work, not release approval.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 20. MT Live Output QA Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 Decision: Current MT live outputs fail MT-V5 output-specificity QA.
\f1\b0 \
The supplied outputs preserve the historic MT structural anchor: Acting and Song components are shown, Vocal remains visible where singing exists, and Acting remains visible where spoken acting exists. That part can remain protected and closed.\
The outputs fail the later v5 standard on enforcement. The main failures are repeated generic MT praise, weak acting-through-song anchoring, vocal feedback that remains technique-heavy or broad, underproduced timestamps across all supplied multi-component reports, unsupported callback/recall/workshop/castability claims, a fixed/submitted-material alternative-repertoire leak, and one critical brief/no-brief contradiction with readiness inconsistency.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 21. Reusable Handoff Pack for Implementation Planning / QA Rerun\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Musical Theatre live-output QA reviewed four current PDF/report artefacts: MT-V5-LIVE-A01 \'93Hannah\'94 score 91, MT-V5-LIVE-A02 \'93Test\'94 score 93 with a brief/no-brief contradiction, MT-V5-LIVE-A03 \'93Test\'94 score 93 with callback/page-side claims, and MT-V5-LIVE-A04 \'93test\'94 score 89 with castability/workshop language. All four preserve the core MT component structure: Acting Scene and Song are displayed, Vocal remains visible where singing exists, and Acting remains visible where spoken acting exists. The stabilised MT anchor is therefore still present in the supplied artefacts.\
The outputs nevertheless fail MT-V5 output-specificity QA. The main repeated failures are generic MT praise, unanchored acting-through-song claims, broad vocal praise, timestamp underproduction, and overconfident live-room/casting claims. Examples include \'93recall-worthy\'94, \'93strong callback potential\'94, \'93highly castable\'94, \'93emotionally connected\'94, \'93strong vocal control\'94, \'93grounded acting\'94, \'93technically excellent\'94, \'93perfect submission\'94, and \'93flawlessly adheres\'94. These phrases often appear without lyric-, phrase-, beat-, style-, addressee-, transition- or component-specific evidence.\
The most serious artefact-level failure is MT-V5-LIVE-A02. It is labelled \'93Brief-driven mode\'94 while its technical signals say \'93No brief \'97 baseline rubric\'94. It also shows Strong for this level and \'93send with confidence\'94 while displaying \'93WHY THIS ISN\'92T READY\'94 and a medium casting-compliance risk based on an unsupported 246s/240s time-limit claim. This creates both brief/no-brief and readiness/verdict contradictions.\
Timestamp density is a cross-output problem. A01 has 2 notes, A02 has 3, A03 has 4, and A04 has 3. For assessable multi-component MT reports around 3\'965 minutes, the MT-V5 target is 5\'968 notes with coverage across acting, song and integration/style where possible. None of the four supplied outputs meets that target.\
Required follow-up is P0: re-run MT outputs after output-rule enforcement, supply raw JSON for each report, provide comparison-page artefacts, provide rendered/export parity artefacts, and verify score/verdict/cap consistency. Additional tests must cover no-brief MT, fixed-material MT, song-only and acting-only negative cases, access-adapted MT, callback/castability suppression and timestamp parity. The MT source/revision branch remains closed; the open work is output enforcement and live QA, not new research or rubric rewrite.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0
